In this critical role, you will conduct credit reviews for new and existing customers and serve as the primary point of contact for escalations involving complex billing and collection issues. You will also lead key accounting close processes, ensuring accurate reporting and financial integrity for our Credit & Collections functions.

You will partner closely with Billing, Revenue Accounting, RevOps, Sales, Legal, Finance and Treasury to optimize cash flow while maintaining best-in-class customer relationships.

This role reports to the Manager, Credit & Collections.

In This Role:

• Month-End Close & Accounting Support: complete month-end close activities for Credit & Collections, including bad debt reserve analysis, sub-ledger reconciliations, and flux analysis.

• Collections & Escalation Management: Own direct collection activity on the highest-exposure, most operationally complex accounts.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Sales, RevOps, Billing, Legal, and Finance to structure complex deals, flag pre-bill issues, and identify and drive resolution of billing discrepancies that delay payment.

• Process Improvement & AI Integration: Identify gaps in the order-to-cash process and implement automation, AI-driven enhancements, or policy changes to improve scalability and efficiency.

• Advanced Excel skills, with the ability to build and maintain complex reporting models and dashboards.

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or related field.

jobs.title: Wholesale Sales Associate
jobs.description:
Revivn is a profitable and rapidly growing company that helps enterprises manage their technology through our end of life software platform. We take electronic recycling one step further by repurposing hardware that still has remaining life and providing it to people who lack dedicated computer access and make it more affordable for people who may not be able to purchase new technology. Working with companies like Instacart, Lyft, Qualtrics, X, Gensler, and Spotify, we are changing the way companies view used technology with a new model that focuses on repurposing instead of recycling.

We’re looking for an ITAD Wholesale Sales Specialist who will be responsible for driving wholesale revenue by sourcing buyers, pricing equipment, and supporting go-to-market teams with competitive inbound valuations. Based out of our Brooklyn, NY office, this role works closely with facility operations to move a diverse mix of IT assets — with a focus on higher-end laptops and related equipment — through the appropriate wholesale channels. The position requires a strong understanding of secondary market pricing, active buyer relationship management, and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, inventory-driven environment.

Please note this role is based on-site at our Brooklyn Navy Yard office with Remote Wednesdays.

What You’ll Do

• Wholesale Sales & Buyer Development Identify, prospect, and onboard new wholesale buyers across relevant secondary market channels Maintain and grow relationships with existing buyers to drive repeat business and volume Negotiate pricing and terms to maximize recovery value on outbound wholesale lots Pricing & Market Intelligence Price outgoing wholesale inventory based on market conditions, equipment grade, and channel demand Provide timely and competitive pricing to go-to-market and inbound valuation teams to support client acquisition and quoting Monitor secondary market trends to ensure pricing remains aligned with current demand Inventory & Channel Alignment Coordinate with facility operations to maintain visibility into available inventory and upcoming material flow Support proper segmentation and allocation of assets to the appropriate wholesale channels Ensure accurate representation of inventory condition, spec, and quantity in all buyer-facing communications Order Management & Fulfillment Support Manage wholesale orders from commitment through shipment, coordinating with internal teams as needed Resolve order exceptions, discrepancies, and buyer inquiries in a timely manner Maintain accurate records of sales activity, buyer accounts, and transaction history Operational Continuity & Process Improvement Support documentation and standardization of wholesale sales processes and pricing frameworks Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, recovery rates, and buyer experience Escalate recurring inventory, pricing, or fulfillment issues to leadership as needed

What We Are Looking For

• 2+ years of experience in ITAD, wholesale sales, or secondary market/re-commerce operations

• Demonstrated ability to develop buyer relationships and close wholesale deals

• Working knowledge of IT asset types, specifications, and grading — particularly laptops and mobile devices

• Strong understanding of secondary market pricing dynamics

• Excellent communication, negotiation, and organizational skills

Bonus

• Experience providing inbound pricing or valuations in an ITAD or re-commerce environment

• Familiarity with ERP, inventory management, or wholesale trading platforms

• Existing network of wholesale buyers in the IT asset space

If this sounds like you, apply! If you don’t meet all of the qualifications but think you could be a good match, we’d still love the chance to review your application.

jobs.title: Principal System Architect
jobs.description:
Primary Work Location

Lincoln, NE or Remote in the U.S.

Overview

The Principal System Architect provides technical direction and hands-on engineering for LI-COR Environmental's connected products and cloud platforms. This individual contributor works across instruments, firmware, connectivity, cloud services, data, and applications to build systems that are reliable, secure, scalable, supportable, and economically sustainable. The architect partners with engineering, product, science, quality, IT and DevOps, and external technology partners to turn complex needs into practical technical direction.

Professional Qualifications

Education

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent demonstrated experience. A master's degree is preferred.

Qualifications

• Typically 12 or more years of software and cloud engineering experience, including significant experience as a system, solution, platform, or principal architect for production systems.

• Demonstrated architecture ownership for a commercial IoT, connected device, industrial, scientific, telemetry, or other high volume data platform.

• Deep experience with AWS or a comparable public cloud, including compute, containers, networking, databases, storage, identity and access, observability, security, resiliency, and infrastructure as code.

• Strong backend engineering and API design skills, with hands-on proficiency in at least one modern backend language.

• Experience with event driven and distributed systems, device ingestion, message delivery, high volume time series data, data modeling, and data lifecycle management.

• Experience with CI/CD, automated testing, observability, incident response, and secure software delivery at production scale.

• Ability to connect architecture decisions to delivery effort, operational cost, product economics, and customer impact.

• Strong communication, technical judgment, systems thinking, and the ability to lead through influence across teams and external partners.

Preferred Experience

• Architecture spanning embedded devices or firmware, cellular or gateway connectivity, cloud ingestion, web or mobile applications, and analytics.

• Regulated, validated, or quality controlled systems with requirements for data access, retention, privacy, auditability, and change control.

• Platform modernization, microservice simplification, globally distributed teams, or blended employee and contractor delivery models.

• Professional level cloud certification or equivalent practical expertise.

General

• Self starter and motivated. Enjoy challenges. Proven drive to achieve goals.

• Creative. High insight, curiosity and problem solving ability. High attention to detail.

• Good interpersonal and networking skills.

• Team player. Enjoys and works well with other people in a team environment.

• Effective oral and written communication skills in English.

• Dependable, positive attitude and good attendance.

• High ethics, integrity, honesty, patience.

Position Responsibilities

Architecture and Platform Direction:

• Define and maintain the target architecture, system boundaries, data models, integration patterns, and technical roadmap for connected products and cloud platforms.

• Lead architecture reviews for services, APIs, data pipelines, databases, identity, applications, deployment patterns, and device-to-cloud communication.

• Simplify the platform by identifying unnecessary coupling, duplicate processing, fragile patterns, and services that should be consolidated, redesigned, or retired.

• Guide platform modernization and the use of managed cloud services based on product needs, customer continuity, cost, portability, security, reliability, and operational burden.

• Maintain architecture decisions and documentation so LI-COR retains the knowledge, access, data portability, and technical control needed to make sound future decisions.

Device to Cloud Architecture:

• Guide how devices produce data and how cloud services receive, process, store, and present it, including schemas, batching, retries, deduplication, derived data, and retention.

• Partner with Firmware and Hardware Engineering to identify connectivity, scalability, reliability, support, and cost implications early in product development.

• Review new products and sensor integrations for downstream effects on cloud services, storage, analytics, applications, and cost-to-serve.

Reliability Security and Operations:

• Define end-to-end observability and nonfunctional requirements for availability, performance, security, privacy, scalability, recovery, and supportability.

• Partner with Engineering and IT and DevOps on CI/CD, infrastructure as code, release architecture, incident response, disaster recovery, vulnerability remediation, and operational readiness.

• Provide technical leadership during significant incidents and recurring performance or connectivity issues, driving root cause correction and durable improvement.

• Ensure platform designs support applicable validation, data separation, retention, privacy, auditability, and customer contractual requirements.

Technical Leadership:

• Serve as a technical partner to the Software and Cloud leader and as an architecture authority across engineering, product, science, quality, and operations.

• Remain hands-on through backend design and implementation, prototypes, technical investigations, code reviews, and resolution of high risk production issues.

• Translate product intent into technically complete approaches and communicate tradeoffs, risks, costs, and recommendations to technical teams and business leaders.

• Mentor engineers and strengthen architecture capability across employees and partners so knowledge and decision quality do not depend on one person.

• Act as LI-COR's technical counterpart with cloud, data, connectivity, and engineering partners while business leaders retain commercial and contract authority.

General

• Periodic travel to LI-COR locations, partner sites, or team working sessions may be required.

• Other job related duties as assigned.

jobs.title: Technical Customer Engineer (Product Support)
jobs.description:
Team: Customer Success / Engineering

Mindset: Do you like writing code to solve customer problems? Read on.

About Nametag

Nametag is a category leader in identity verification, security, and account protection. We are building a world-class, remote-first team where engineers thrive in both technical depth and customer engagement. We value intellectual curiosity, collaboration, and a strong sense of responsibility in protecting enterprise security.

About the Role

We’re hiring a Technical Customer Engineer to serve as the technical escalation point for customer-reported issues. This is an engineering-adjacent role focused on diagnosing complex integration problems, scripting and prototyping solutions, and collaborating directly with our core engineering team to drive fixes into production.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys debugging, writing lightweight code, and working closely with customers to unblock them quickly. This goes beyond ticket processing - it’s hands-on technical problem solving with real ownership.

Responsibilities

• Act as the first technical responder for escalated customer issues, particularly those blocking integrations or deployments.

• Debug in the wild - inspecting API payloads, webhook logs, OAuth exchanges, and race conditions that surface only under real-world load.

• Provide interim solutions such as code snippets, pull requests, documentation updates, or configuration guidance.

• Bridge the gap between customer and engineering: reproduce issues, isolate root causes, and ensure fixes are fully validated before release.

• Gather structured context and relay actionable insights to engineering for long-term fixes.

• Recommend integration best practices across authentication flows, REST APIs, and IAM platforms.

• Improve internal support tooling, documentation, and runbooks based on recurring patterns.

• Surface common pain points and influence product priorities.

Tech You’ll Work With

• You need to be comfortable in our primary languages (Go, Typescript), as well as some experience in a few of the other common platforms our customers use (Python, Ruby, that kind of thing).

• REST APIs, OAuth, Webhooks (reference: getnametag.com/docs)

• Authentication and identity workflows (OIDC, SSO, Token Exchanges)

• Scripting or debugging tools in Python, Node.js, Bash, or similar environments

• Identity platforms: Okta, Microsoft Entra, Duo, Auth0, Ping, and custom IAM stacks.

• Systems: AWS, CloudFormation, Postgres, Docker, GitHub Actions, modern observability stacks

Qualifications

Work Authorization (Required): Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without current or future need for visa sponsorship. This is a firm requirement. The technical qualifications below are guidelines.

• 2–5 years in technical support engineering, solutions engineering, DevOps, SRE, or adjacent engineering roles.

• Client facing experience - ability to communicate clearly and empathetically with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Strong debugging skills across APIs, backend integrations, or authentication workflows.

• Comfort writing lightweight scripts or tools to diagnose and unblock issues.

• Familiarity with IAM platforms such as Okta, Microsoft Entra, Duo, or similar.

Who Will Succeed in This Role If

• You like solving real customer problems more than sitting behind abstract tickets.

• You don’t mind hopping between console logs, Slack threads, and cURL commands.

• You stay calm when something is broken, and you don’t stop until it’s understood.

Why Join

You’ll join a fast-moving team where customer impact is immediate and visible. You’ll collaborate directly with engineering leadership, shape how we scale technical support, and build a reputation as a go-to problem solver.

If you’re the person others call when things break - let’s talk.

Compensation & Benefits

• Competitive salary: $120,000 - $160,000

• Potential equity in a high-growth company

• Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)

• Flexible time off policies

• 401(k) program with employer matching

• Remote-first culture with opportunities for in-person collaboration during quarterly team off-sites

jobs.title: Project Controls Specialist I, Cost Analysis
jobs.location: Charlotte, North Carolina; Durham, North Carolina
jobs.description:
At gFiber, we believe that great internet has the power to drive innovation, strengthen communities, enable the impossible, and do all the everyday things that make all of our world go round. And the job of creating better internet is never done - so we’re growing! Our team is committed to building a place where people who want to make a difference can grow their careers and find their spot to belong.

The application window will be open until at least September 28th, 2026. This opportunity will remain online based on business needs which may be before or after the specified date.

Role Description (and additional job description)

As a Project Controls Specialist, Cost Analysis, you play a critical role in partnering with the Project Controls Managers and Field Operations Organization team to ensure our ambitious construction projects are delivered on time and on budget. In this role, you will use your organizational skills to ensure that projects are delivered systematically and problem-solving skills to identify and drive improvements in our process to make sure that projects are highly controlled. You will also use data to guide your recommendations. More specific to this role, you will also be the team expert in project control cost tooling and processes. This means you will develop the standards, oversee rollout and training of new cost tools and processes, manage our cost control support vendors, and be the cost control SME and liaison between stakeholders and business partners.

In this role, you'll:

• Support the regional and metro specific project controls, accounting, and technical operations teams as the central point of contact for cost control.

• Partner with Project Controls Managers and cross functional partners through training and regular office hours to ensure alignment across regional team members.

• Identify process inefficiencies, assess risk, and create solutions that allow for the central implementation of budgets, controls and schedules for a centralized projects controls team.

• Provide financial support through monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting, including cost analysis and variance reporting to drive business insights and resource planning.

• Support development of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial projections and reports based on analysis of consumption and productivity data then work with cross-functional partners to ensure regular monthly reconciliations, spend governance, reviews, and approvals.

At a minimum we'd like you to have:

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

• 2 years of experience in project controls, construction coordination, cost analysis, or related roles.

• Experience working with spreadsheets, especially for data reconciliation, insight generation and process improvements.

• Experience analyzing raw data and translating it into actionable insights or summaries.

It's preferred if you have:

• Experience in project management, finance and accounting processes and terminology.

• Experience with scheduling software and best practices (e.g., Microsoft Project, Asana, Smartsheet).

• Knowledge of Actual Cost of work performed.

• Knowledge of expended cost on a project, knowledge of project delivery, project close out, project reporting.

• Exposure to ISP networks and technical deployment.

• Experience working with cross-functional teams.

The US base hourly range for this full-time position is between $28.61 - $34.76 + bonus + benefits. As pay varies by location, your recruiter will share more about the specific hourly range for your targeted location during the hiring process.

jobs.title: FAST Support Analyst
jobs.description:
About TEGNA

TEGNA Inc. helps people thrive in their local communities by providing the trusted local news and services that matter most. With 64 television stations in 51 U.S. markets, TEGNA reaches more than 100 million people monthly across the web, mobile apps, streaming, and linear television. Together, we are building a sustainable future for local news.

The FAST Workflow Analyst is responsible for supporting the day-to-day operation, monitoring, troubleshooting, and distribution of live and linear content feeds for TEGNA to Free Ad-Supported Television (FAST) platforms and other streaming partners. This role serves as a key point of contact between internal streaming and technology teams, local stations, FAST partners, vendors, and development teams to ensure feeds are available, reliable, correctly configured, and delivered according to established distribution requirements.

Responsibilities:
•    Monitor and operate FAST distribution and 24/7 streaming workflows to ensure feeds remain available, content plays as scheduled, and streams are delivered reliably to FAST partners and digital platforms. Monitor stream health, content continuity, audio/video quality, slates, interruptions, and other issues that may impact the viewer experience. – 25%
•    Troubleshoot, triage, and manage streaming and FAST distribution incidents from initial detection through resolution. Investigate issues across station, cloud, streaming, distribution, and partner environments; determine scope and impact; coordinate escalation; communicate status; and ensure incidents are resolved within established service expectations. – 25%
•    Support FAST distribution operations and partner relationships, including onboarding new feeds, testing and validating feeds, coordinating configuration changes, troubleshooting partner delivery issues, supporting feed migrations, and working directly with FAST partners and vendors to resolve service-impacting issues. – 15%
•    Implement and maintain monitoring, alerting, and operational tools across streaming and FAST distribution platforms to proactively identify failures and performance issues. Analyze monitoring data and recurring alerts to improve detection, reduce mean time to detect (MTTD), and reduce mean time to restore (MTTR). – 10%
•    Partner with station engineering, digital, streaming, application, and infrastructure teams to support end-to-end workflows from content origination through streaming and FAST distribution. Assist with capacity planning, workflow changes, platform migrations, technology implementations, and projects that improve reliability and scalability. – 10%
•    Document end-to-end streaming and FAST distribution workflows, including feed configurations, partner requirements, troubleshooting procedures, escalation paths, and operational runbooks. Maintain knowledge base articles and enable effective Service Desk escalation and self-service where appropriate. – 5%
•    Maintain accurate inventories and operational information for streaming feeds, FAST channels, applications, services, integrations, configurations, and versions within the ServiceNow CMDB or other designated systems to support reporting, lifecycle management, troubleshooting, and incident response. – 5%
•    Analyze incidents, operational trends, and partner feedback to identify recurring issues and opportunities for process, workflow, tooling, automation, or architecture improvements that increase reliability and improve the viewer and partner experience.
•    Support special projects, major events, new technology implementations, and evolving streaming initiatives as assigned. Participate in testing and validation of new workflows and constructively challenge existing processes to improve reliability, efficiency, and scalability. – 2%

Requirements:
•    College degree, relevant certifications, or equivalent practical experience in broadcast, media technology, or IT operations.
•    Hands-on experience supporting broadcast, newsroom, and streaming technologies, such as Cuez, AWS media services, including AWS Elemental MediaConnect and MediaLive.
•    Working knowledge of cloud and hybrid environments supporting media workflows (e.g., cloud-based contribution, streaming, monitoring, or playout).
•    Strong understanding of IT service management concepts and tooling, including ITIL practices, incident/problem management, knowledge management, CMDBs, and ServiceNow.
•    Proven ability to manage multiple operational priorities simultaneously, particularly in live production or time-sensitive environments.
•    Clear communicator who can translate technical issues into business and operational impact for engineers, newsroom staff, digital teams, vendors, and leadership.
•    Analytical, methodical problem solver with the ability to diagnose complex issues across systems, networks, applications, and workflows.

Benefits:

TEGNA offers comprehensive benefits designed to safeguard the physical, mental and financial health of our employees and their families. TEGNA offers two medical plan options for full and part-time employees through Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas, as well as access to dental and eye care coverage; fertility, surrogacy and adoption assistance; disability and life insurance.

Our 401(k) program offers full, part-time and temporary employees the opportunity to contribute 1% - 80% of their pay on a pre-tax basis to TEGNA’s 401(k). Contributions made up to the first 4% of pay are eligible for a 100% match from the company and are 100% vested from day one.

Regardless of participation in TEGNA medical plans, ALL employees and their eligible family members receive nine free virtual doctor’s appointments with a physician through Teladoc, and 12 free annual therapy sessions with a licensed clinician through Spring Health.

TEGNA offers a generous Paid Time Off (PTO) benefit as well as nine paid holidays per year.

* Some jobs are covered by a collective bargaining agreement and thus some or all of the benefits described herein may not apply. For example, some newsroom bargaining unit employees receive health and retirement benefits under plans administered by the union.

EEO statement:

TEGNA Inc. is a proud equal opportunity employer. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, hiring and developing individuals from diverse backgrounds and experiences to add to our collaborative culture. We value and consider applications from all qualified candidates without regard to actual or perceived race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, age, marital status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, family responsibilities, disability, medical condition, enrollment in college or vocational school, political affiliation, military or veteran status, citizenship status, genetic information, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law. TEGNA will reasonably accommodate qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with applicable law. If you are in need of an accommodation in order to submit your application, please email askhr@tegna.com

Recruiting Fraud Alert:

To all candidates: your personal information and online safety are important to us. Only TEGNA Recruiters or Hiring Managers will reach out to you regarding consideration of your application or background.  Communications with TEGNA employees will either come from a TEGNA email address with a domain of tegna.com or one of our affiliate station domains.

Recruiters or Hiring Managers will never request payments, ask for financial account information or sensitive information such as social security numbers.

jobs.title: Payments Operations Analyst
jobs.description:
Tabs is the AI Operating System for Revenue, built for modern finance and accounting teams. It combines deep revenue and accounting expertise with the agents and applications needed to run revenue work end to end. Tabs understands customer and contract context, applies accounting logic, and executes critical workflows with built in controls, auditability, and human oversight. With Tabs, finance teams can move from manually managing revenue workflows to directing outcomes while the system executes the work.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Payments Operations Analyst to execute day-to-day operations and support the scaling of Tabs' payments program as we bring payments in-house. You will work directly with our Senior Payments Operations Lead, helping to manage merchant operations, disputes, reconciliation, and exceptions as Tabs Pay launches and grows.

You'll be hands-on and detail-oriented, executing defined workflows and improving them incrementally. This role is ideal for someone who takes pride in making processes work reliably, escalating issues appropriately, and identifying practical bottlenecks. You'll be the first responder on operational issues and own a meaningful portion of our day-to-day PayOps work.

Tabs Pay serves large North American B2B merchants across an ACH-first payment mix with a growing card share. Operational accuracy and attention to detail directly protect merchant relationships and Tabs' financial integrity.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Process merchant exceptions, holds, reserve adjustments, and merchant activation according to defined policies and documented procedures.

 - Execute daily and periodic reconciliation across processor, bank, ledger, and merchant-settlement records; identify and escalate breaks for investigation or resolution.

 - Manage the dispute and chargeback workflow: collect merchant evidence, track deadlines, ensure timely submissions, and follow up on outcomes.

 - Process ACH returns and negative-balance events according to documented timelines and procedures.

 - Investigate and resolve merchant-reported operational issues and discrepancies within your authority; escalate appropriately.

 - Monitor ongoing merchant activity against policy thresholds; flag merchants requiring review or adjustment.

 - Keep process runbooks, decision trees, checklists, and operational logs current and usable by the team.

 - Identify operational inefficiencies and bottlenecks; document observations and bring improvement recommendations to leadership.

 - Track operational KPIs and metrics; prepare regular reporting on PayOps status and performance.

 - Support cross-functional work with Finance, Engineering, Support, and commercial teams to implement operational changes and new tooling.
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3–5 years of experience in payments operations, reconciliation, dispute management, merchant operations, or an adjacent operational function.

 - Demonstrated execution of payments workflows (reconciliation, dispute processing, ACH returns, merchant management, exception handling) at a payment facilitator, processor, platform, or fintech.

 - Strong track record of accurate, detail-oriented work in high-stakes operational environments where errors cascade downstream.

 - Ability to follow defined processes consistently and identify practical improvements without constant oversight.

 - Clear judgment about which issues require escalation and which can be resolved independently; structured communication about decisions and outcomes.

 - Comfort prioritizing among competing operational tasks and managing your own queue of work.

 - Effective collaboration with support, finance, product, and operational partners to understand requirements and implement changes.

 - Comfort with defined processes and strong operational discipline; appreciation for documentation and systematic approach to work.

 - Familiarity with card payment operations (chargebacks, disputes, settlement mechanics) OR strong ACH expertise with willingness to learn card operations; we're flexible on depth depending on your payment rails background.

 - Comfort learning and adopting new tools, including automation and AI-enabled operational tools, to improve accuracy and efficiency.




HELPFUL EXPERIENCE

 - B2B payments, billing, or invoicing platforms.

 - Merchant underwriting, reserve monitoring, or risk-related support workflows.

 - ACH or card payment operations, including return and chargeback handling.

 - Finance operations, customer success operations, or customer support with payments exposure.

 - Experience working with payment processors, acquirers, or banking partners.

 - Familiarity with reconciliation tooling, payment APIs, or transaction data management.

 - Cross-border payments, multi-currency flows, or international money movement.

 - Experience with automation tools or AI-enabled operational workflows.
   
   


ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

This role is based in New York City, 5 days a week at our Soho office.




PERKS AND BENEFITS (FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES)

 - Competitive compensation and equity

 - Unlimited PTO

 - Up to 100% employer covered monthly healthcare premium (medical, dental, vision)

 - Lunch provided via Sharebite, plus dinner for any later in office days.

 - Parental leave up to 12 weeks

 - Tax free commuter and parking benefits

 - Voluntary insurances (Life, Hospital, Critical Illness, Accident)

 - Employee Assistance Program (Rightway)

 - Free One Medical Membership

 - 401k

Tabs is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome teammates of all identities and do not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. We’re committed to creating an environment where everyone can grow, contribute, and feel comfortable being themselves.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer- Facilities
jobs.description:
Renesas is seeking a Staff Mechanical Engineer to support and lead facilities engineering activities across its company‑owned 120‑acre semiconductor manufacturing campus, comprising approximately 528,000 square feet of controlled indoor space across six buildings supporting wafer fabrication, testing, and critical support operations.

This role provides technical ownership and leadership for complex mechanical systems essential to semiconductor manufacturing, including HVAC, process piping, plumbing, fire protection systems, and the Industrial / DI Water Plant. The Staff Mechanical Engineer will partner closely with operations, maintenance, construction, and external vendors to ensure high system reliability, regulatory compliance, cost control, and long‑term campus sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Facilities Mechanical Engineering & System Ownership

• Provide engineering leadership and technical ownership for facilities mechanical systems, including:HVAC systems supporting cleanroom and manufacturing environmentsProcess and utility piping systemsPlumbing and fire suppression systemsIndustrial Water and DI Water Plant systems
• Evaluate system performance, capacity, and reliability to support current operations and future manufacturing requirements
• Develop short‑term and long‑term facilities strategies aligned with site and business growth plans

Design, Documentation & Engineering Standards

• Lead mechanical system design efforts, including development of:Engineering drawings and layoutsSpecifications and design criteriaCost estimates and capital justifications
• Perform and/or review AutoCAD drafting, drawings, and specifications
• Review and approve materials, equipment submittals, and contractor documentation
• Maintain accurate as‑built drawings, engineering records, and system documentation for all assigned facilities assets

Operations, Maintenance & Troubleshooting Support

• Partner with operations and maintenance teams to:Troubleshoot complex mechanical system issuesImprove system uptime, efficiency, and reliabilityOptimize maintenance strategies and lifecycle costs
• Provide technical guidance during system failures, upgrades, and major maintenance events

Project Management & Construction Oversight

• Plan, manage, and execute capital and expense-funded facilities projects
• Coordinate with internal stakeholders, contractors, and consultants to ensure project execution meets:Engineering drawings and specificationsContractual requirementsBudget and schedule commitments
• Oversee construction activities to ensure safe execution and quality installation

Code Compliance & Safety

• Ensure all mechanical systems and projects comply with applicable:Life safety codesLocal, state, and federal regulationsCompany engineering standards and policies
• Support audits, inspections, and regulatory reviews as required

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
• Minimum 5 years of engineering experience in an industrial and/or manufacturing environment (semiconductor, high‑tech manufacturing, power generation, or similar facilities preferred)
• Demonstrated experience supporting mechanical facilities systems such as HVAC, piping, and industrial utilities
• Strong working knowledge of engineering drawings, specifications, and construction practices
• Ability to independently lead projects and resolve complex technical issues

Applicants for this position must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Renesas is unable to sponsor applicants for work visas for this position now or in the future.

• 100% onsite position, Monday through Friday

Renesas is an embedded semiconductor solution provider driven by its Purpose, To Make Our Lives Easier. With a global team of over 21,000 engineers and problem solvers in more than 30 countries, we offer the opportunity to work on world‑leading technology for Automotive, Industrial, Infrastructure, and IoT, shaping a safer, healthier, greener, and smarter future.

At Renesas, TAGIE is our culture, grounded in being Transparent, Agile, Global, Innovative, and Entrepreneurial. It shapes how we work, grow and deliver on our purpose together. This collaborative spirit and mindset drive our semiconductor technology to transform industries and impact millions of lives.

We believe in rewarding our employees with a competitive benefits package alongside their salary. More information will be provided during the hiring process.

Are you ready to join our team and shape the future with us?

jobs.description:
Pionnier des ventes événementielles en ligne depuis 2001 et acteur incontournable du e-commerce en Europe, Veepee collabore avec plus de 7 000 marques pour proposer des produits à forte décote, disponibles sur une durée limitée. Présent dans de nombreux univers parmi lesquels la mode, la maison, le vin, le voyage, ou encore la beauté ... Veepee a réalisé en 2024 un chiffre d’affaires de 3,3 milliards d’euros TTC et compte 5 000 collaborateurs répartis dans 10 pays.
 
Le Comptable achats négoce (Purchase Accountant) est rattaché à la Direction financière et au département Brand payment. 
Sous la supervision du Responsable d'équipe, il est en charge des flux financiers et comptables des comptes fournisseurs.
Il a pour missions principales d’assurer la tenue des comptes fournisseurs, de la prise en charge des factures à la réconciliation de compte ainsi que du traitement financier des stocks.
Il travaille en collaboration avec l’ensemble des métiers transverses en Business Unit.
Activités principales
Activité 1 : Gestion du contrôle des Bons de commandes dans l’outil financier (SAP) en assurant les vérifications : 
Des informations fournisseurs (Adresses, N°TVA, RIB à jour, …)
Du flux de marchandises (Company code)
De la bonne cohérence des montants entre la donnée existante dans l’outil et le bon de commande transmis par les équipes Supply Chain
Activité 2 : Contrôle et traitement de la facture
Réception de la facture via portail électronique / courrier / Emails 
Contrôle de la conformité de la facture (champs légaux : N°TVA, bonnes entités, Taux de TVA,..)
Enregistrement de la facture
Emission d’un possible paiement d’acompte en fonction des conditions négociées
Activité 3 : Gestion des retours et des pièces comptables associées
Envoi de l’état définitif de la réception et de l’expédition en entrepôt avec les demandes d’avoirs correspondantes
Emission des documents comptables (facturation des pénalités et divers prestations de services)
Tenue du compte fournisseur (relance et suivi des pièces comptables en cohérence avec la demande des documents)  
Gestion des retours selon la préconisation commerciale (renvoi ou rachat)
Récupération des données fournisseurs (adresse, contact, RMA, EORI…) 
Communication à la marque des détails sur les retours membres avec la demande d’avoir correspondante
Suivi des retours jusqu’à la livraison


Activité 4 : Analyser le solde de l’opération au niveau comptable et s’assurer du paiement à la marque 
Récupération des différentes pièces comptables essentielles à l’élaboration du soldes (factures et avoirs)
Analyse et comptabilisation des écarts entre les factures et les provisions
Gestion des litiges avec les différents services concernés (Supply, Commerce, Logistique, Transport)
Etablissement du paiement final
Lettrage du compte, réconciliation avec fournisseurs, ajustement des écarts comptables
Synthèse du compte à la fin de vente
Ce descriptif de poste est non exhaustif et les missions du salarié sont susceptibles d’évoluer.
Relations internes / externes
Relations externes : partenaires (marques)  
Relations internes: relation en transverse avec l’ensemble des interlocuteurs (Sourcing, Entrepôts, Supply et Finances)

Formation et expérience professionnelles 
Requises pour la fonction et non celle du titulaire
Niveau et type de formation initiale : Bac+2/3 ou équivalent en Comptabilité
Expérience professionnelle (type et durée) : 3 à 4 ans sur un poste similaire

Rigueur, 
Sens de l’analyse
Orientation résultats, solution et résolution de problèmes
Organisation et gestion des priorités
Gestion du stress et de l’urgence
Sens du service
Autonomie
Qualités relationnelles et rédactionnelles
 
Compétences techniques
Maîtrise de SAP
Maîtrise du PackOffice (Excel) et de la Google Suite

jobs.title: Warehouse Support
jobs.location: St. Louis Park, MN, United States
jobs.description:
Eurofins is searching for a Warehouse Support Associate in St Louis Park, MN Metro Area

The Warehouse Support position is responsible for the pick-up and delivery of water, soil and air samples to and from the service center. The Warehouse Support team maintains the quality, hold time, and turnaround time objectives of the lab, as well as prepares and delivers bottle orders to clients following the SOP of the lab. This team will also oversee receiving and stocking of all sample control supplies and prepare/ship sample kits utilizing the Eurofins LIMs system (TALs).

Warehouse Support responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

• Performs all duties as outlined in the SOP for Couriers.
• Picks up and delivers samples, bottle orders, etc. to the service center.
• Counts the number of samples when receiving them from clients to make sure that the Chain of Custody and samples match. Verifies that samples are not broken or damaged.
• Receives and sign the Chain of Custody.
• Ensures that client signs, dates, and records time on the Chain of Custody when releasing samples.
• Transports samples on ice from client site to the service center, or from our service center to a sub-contracted laboratory.
• Unloads samples and inspect for damage or violated hold times to maintain sample integrity.
• Interacts with Project Managers and clients appropriately and professionally.
• Follows directions or use maps to locate client offices/sites as specified in the courier request form.
• Communicates effectively with coworkers about the courier routes and schedule.
• Records in the courier log book the time that courier arrives to the site and time leaving from the site for all the pick ups and deliveries.
• Maintains records for the vehicle maintenance and driving miles; turn it in at the end of each month.
• Restocks supplies when received so supplies are available to employees when needed.
• Verifies the validity and completeness of all bottle orders being delivered. This verification is done prior to leaving for delivery.
• Performs duties in accordance with Section 14 of the Transportation and Fleet Safety of the Corporate Safety Manual.
• Complies with the Company’s “Driver Evaluation and Qualification Policy”.
• Maintains the shipping/receiving area to ensure a safe work environment.
• Prepares outgoing shipments of bottle kits and outgoing coolers of samples for delivery to laboratory.
• Utilizes Eurofins LIMS system (TALs) to receive bottle orders from project managers and prepare them in kits as directed.
• Maintains delivery vehicle to keep in proper working order.
• May be assigned other sample control duties as identified by the Service Center Manager.

The ideal candidate would possess:

• Ability to read maps and follow directions
• Ability to operate a motor vehicle
• Ability to prioritize
• Excellent communication (oral and written) and attention to detail
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team, self-motivation, adaptability, and a positive attitude
• Ability to learn new techniques, perform multiple tasks simultaneously, keep accurate records, follow instructions, and comply with company policies
• Skills to utilize a company phone for communication with clients and coworkers as well as provide copies of COCs to laboratory personnel and support the eCOC initiative

Basic Minimum Qualifications:

• High school diploma or equivalent
• Valid Driver's License
• Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship

Candidates currently living within a commutable distance of St. Louis Park, MN Metro are encouraged to apply.

Hours for Position: M-F 9 AM- 5 PM

To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com.

We support your development! Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity! Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us! We are well on our way to achieving our objective of carbon neutrality by 2025, through a combination of emission reduction and compensation initiatives. We encourage our laboratory leaders to make sustainable changes at their local level, and in addition to their initiatives we also count on our dedicated carbon reduction team to help us to achieve this goal!

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Company description: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and Eurofins Scientific 2/2 March 2023 agroscience contract research services. jobs.title: Senior Manager, Spectrum Licensing
jobs.description:
Why LeoLabs?

At LeoLabs, we're building the living map of activity in space. Through our proprietary global radar network and AI-enabled analytics platform, we collect millions of measurements daily on more than 25,000 objects in low Earth orbit (LEO). Our radar-powered intelligence protects billions in assets, monitors adversarial behavior, and ensures safe operations for commercial and government missions.

We're not just building technology, we are redefining global security, safety, and transparency in space. As orbital activity accelerates and threats grow more complex, LeoLabs is a trusted partner for Space Domain Awareness, Space Traffic Management, and Satellite Operations for top-tier space operators and allied defense organizations.

If you're looking to work on mission-critical challenges at the forefront of aerospace, national security, and AI, your impact starts here.

The Opportunity

LeoLabs is expanding its global network of ground-based radars, and securing the Radio Frequency regulatory approvals required to deploy and operate those systems is critical to that growth. In this role, you will lead LeoLabs' global RF permitting function, owning the operational strategy and execution for spectrum licensing, experimental and permanent operating authorities, equipment certification, and type approval across new and existing markets.

This is a senior RF operations and program leadership role operating at the intersection of RF engineering, government engagement, site selection, and deployment. Some jurisdictions offer clear licensing pathways; others require extensive consultation, local representation, technical studies, and persistence to establish a workable path. You will be accountable for understanding those differences early, translating them into practical plans, and driving approvals to completion.

You will work closely with the Company’s Site Selection and Acquisition team, the Hardware Engineering team, and the Legal Department, as well as testing laboratories, in-country consultants, and other external specialists. This role is based in the United States, with the West Coast strongly preferred, requires regular domestic and international travel, and reports to the Senior Director of Global Infrastructure.

Responsibilities:

• Owning LeoLabs' global RF permitting program and operational strategy for new and existing radar locations, including spectrum licensing, equipment certification requirements in different global jurisdictions, type approval requirements, and related RF regulatory approvals.

• Under the direction of the Legal Department: Collaborating closely with Legal on matters involving interpretation of applicable law, novel or ambiguous legal or regulatory requirements, material legal or regulatory risk, material license conditions or commitments, and regulatory positions that may create legal obligations or significant risk for LeoLabs. Investigating and documenting regulatory requirements and approval pathways for proposed deployments in new countries and jurisdictions, including responsible regulators, application categories, technical evidence, local applicant or representative requirements, testing, fees, lead times, and renewal obligations.

• Developing jurisdiction-specific RF licensing strategies and identifying permitting and implementation risks, dependencies, decision points, and critical-path activities early enough to inform site selection, deployment sequencing, and investment decisions.

• Actively supporting early engagement with spectrum regulators and other government agencies to validate proposed pathways, clarify technical and procedural novel requirements, and reduce the risk of late-stage surprises before formal submissions are made.

• Actively assisting in the preparation of spectrum license applications from feasibility through approval, including preparation of application strategies, technical annexes, supporting studies, regulator responses, license conditions, modifications, and renewals.

• Maintaining LeoLabs’ existing radar-site RF licenses, including tracking license conditions, managing renewals and modifications, and monitoring compliance with operational and technical license requirements.

• Working with LeoLabs' experienced RF engineers and Hardware Engineering team to obtain antenna characteristics, emission parameters, radiation patterns, simulations, interference studies, test data, and other technical evidence required by regulators.

• Owning the coordination of equipment certification and type approval workstreams in jurisdictions where LeoLabs is considering deploying radars. This includes identifying applicable standards, local testing or certification requirements, import-related approvals where applicable, and coordinating with accredited laboratories, certification bodies, and local representatives.

• Integrating RF regulatory considerations into new radar site selection by identifying potential interference or spectrum compatibility concerns and determining when detailed engineering analysis is required.

• Coordinating new site interference analyses and reviews with LeoLabs' RF Engineering team or external specialists when specialist engineering judgement is required.

• Project managing regulatory approvals across multiple countries and deployments, including schedules, budgets, risks, dependencies, consultant deliverables, internal technical inputs, regulator actions, and executive decision points.

• Selecting, briefing, and managing local RF regulatory consultants and technical advisers while retaining internal ownership of RF permitting execution, quality, schedule, and outcomes. Legal will manage legal counsel and advisers engaged to provide legal advice.

• Building and maintaining a global network of spectrum regulators, regulatory advisers, testing laboratories, certification specialists, and in-country contacts who can support LeoLabs' expansion into both straightforward and difficult regulatory environments.

• Establishing scalable processes, templates, checklists, consultant scopes of work, country playbooks, decision records, license trackers, renewal controls, and a central knowledge base for global RF permitting.

• Preparing concise leadership updates and recommendations on RF permitting feasibility, approval probability, schedule, operational and technical risk, mitigation options, and whether a proposed location or licensing strategy should advance, pause, or change.

Required Qualifications

• Located on the U.S. West Coast (Pacific or Mountain time zones)

• 10+ years of experience in spectrum management, RF regulatory operations, RF compliance, telecommunications licensing, or a closely related technical or regulatory field.

• Demonstrated experience obtaining spectrum licenses or equivalent RF operating approvals, including direct engagement with government spectrum regulators.

• Strong working knowledge of RF fundamentals, including frequency allocations, bandwidth, emissions, antenna characteristics, propagation, interference, and spectrum compatibility.

• Demonstrated ability to navigate complex, ambiguous, or novel regulatory environments where the approval pathway is not fully defined at the outset.

• Strong project or program management capability, including schedule, risk, dependency, consultant, budget, and stakeholder management across multiple concurrent workstreams.

• Ability to understand and operationalize regulatory requirements and translate them into clear technical inputs, application requirements, consultant scopes, and internal actions, and to identify matters requiring escalation to Legal or other subject-matter experts.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn incomplete or highly technical information into clear recommendations for senior leadership and external stakeholders.

• Strong judgement and stakeholder management skills, with the credibility to work effectively with regulators, engineers, government officials, consultants, and executives.

• Strong recordkeeping discipline and a high standard for documentation quality, version control, decision logs, license records, and organized project files.

• Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally and undertake field work at prospective radar sites.

• Based in the United States and eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with radar, radiolocation, satellite, aerospace, defense, telecommunications, or other high-power RF systems.

• Experience securing spectrum approvals across multiple countries or regions, including jurisdictions with complex government or regulatory processes.

• Experience with equipment certification, RF/EMC compliance testing, international type approval, or laboratory certification programs.

• Experience conducting RF spectrum surveys using spectrum analyzers, antennas, and associated test equipment and interpreting the resulting data.

• Experience performing or reviewing RF interference, compatibility, propagation, or coexistence analysis.

• Existing international network of spectrum regulators, regulatory consultants, testing laboratories, or certification specialists.

• Degree in electrical or RF engineering, telecommunications, physics, or another relevant technical discipline; equivalent practical experience is also valued.

• PMP, PgMP, or equivalent project/program management experience.

Within 3 months, you'll

• Establish the operating model, priorities, reporting cadence, and core standards for LeoLabs' global RF permitting function.

• Review active and planned radar deployments, current license workstreams, consultant engagements, and country-specific regulatory risks, and identify immediate gaps or critical-path actions.

• Build strong working relationships with Radar Engineering, Site Selection and Acquisition, Legal, and other key stakeholders.

• Have reviewed all existing LeoLabs radar-site RF licenses, documented applicable conditions and renewal dates, and established a reliable process for ongoing tracking and operational compliance, modifications and renewals.

Within 6 months, you'll

• Be actively managing the global RF regulatory portfolio with clear country strategies, schedules, risk visibility, decision points, and consultant accountability.

• Have implemented repeatable approaches for preliminary RF surveys, regulatory feasibility assessments, license applications, type approval, document control, and renewal tracking.

• Have expanded LeoLabs' network of trusted local regulatory consultants, laboratories, and government contacts in priority jurisdictions.

Within 12 months, you'll

• Have built a scalable global RF permitting capability that identifies regulatory risk early and supports faster, better-informed radar deployment decisions.

• Have improved the predictability, quality, and schedule control of spectrum licensing and equipment approval workstreams across multiple jurisdictions.

• Have established a durable country knowledge base, external adviser network, and internal operating model that reduces dependency on ad hoc regulatory discovery for each new deployment.

Compensation

The base salary range for this position is up to $203,000 USD + bonus + stock options + benefits

Compensation Note: The salary range for this position is benchmarked based on the designated primary work location for the role. Final compensation may vary depending on the selected candidate's work location, applicable market data, experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors.

Perks and Benefits

• $100 USD monthly wellness benefit to support your health and well-being

• $300 USD home office setup stipend, available for use within your first six months

• $75 USD monthly home internet allowance, paid directly through your regular paycheck

• Individual Development Fund to support training, learning, and professional development

• Employee Recognition Program to celebrate contributions and achievements across the team

ITAR Requirements

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. More information regarding ITAR can be found at DDTC’s website.

Vendor Notification

LeoLabs does not engage external staffing agencies or third-party recruiting firms for this role. Unsolicited candidate submissions will not be considered.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

jobs.title: Clinical Pharmacist Float-Critical Care and ED, Full-time Rotating
jobs.description:
The Clinical Pharmacist reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Clinical Pharmacist is responsible for identifying, preventing, and/or resolving medication related problems; for providing authoritative information to other health care professionals, patients, and the public; and for assuring that the informational, clinical, and drug distribution components of pharmacy services function as an integrated system to provide patient centered care to the patients and staff of Northwestern Medicine.

The mission of the Department of Pharmacy is to deliver the safest, highest quality, most effective and efficient patient care while developing the best people, advancing research, and integrating pharmacy services to successfully coordinate care across the Northwestern Medicine enterprise.

The vision of the Department of Pharmacy is to be a recognized as a national leader in advancing the pharmacy enterprise through excellence, innovation, education and research.

Responsibilities:

• Interprets medication orders to ensure safety and proper use of medications and is alert to compatibilities, incompatibilities, medication duplication, medication allergies, and potential medication administration errors. Coordinates the solving of medication related problems between pharmacy, nursing, and prescribers, demonstrating initiative and sound judgment.
• Monitors medication therapy for significant drug-drug, drug-diet, or drug-laboratory test interactions. Intervenes in circumstances of significant interactions, therapeutic duplications, and other occasions where pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic expertise is warranted.
• Evaluates and documents that the medication(s) selected are appropriate for achieving the desired therapeutic outcome. Communicates potential problems and likely solutions to the prescriber.
• Acts as a consultant in the areas of pharmacokinetics and adverse reactions to physicians, nurses and other healthcare professionals. Participates in all therapeutic drug monitoring or intervention programs; adjusting therapy as indicated by patient condition and laboratory results.
• Processes all medication order information into the Electronic Health Record to ensure accuracy of records regarding past, current and future dispensing and charging.
• Maintains a comprehensive pharmacy patient profile. The profile should include age, maturation, weight, allergies, diagnosis, estimated and actual pharmacokinetic parameters, and pertinent information which may affect medication therapy decisions.
• Oversees the packaging labeling, and distribution of medications for all patients and employees according to established policies, procedures, and guidelines. Monitors the use of scheduled medications on the nursing units and maintains controlled inventories of medication in the dispensing areas.
• Compounds and dispenses pharmaceuticals including sterile products, chemotherapy and parenteral nutrition products.
• Verifies medication orders before delivery to patient care areas and ensures accuracy and completeness. Resolves discrepancies as necessary.
• Reviews all laboratory data for appropriateness of medication use and recommends changes when needed. Including microbial culture and sensitivity data, toxicology, therapeutic drug monitoring, etc.
• Develops and presents orientation, education and training programs for medical, nursing, hospital and pharmacy staff, as well as assisting in the educating of pharmacy students, residents, and fellows.
• Educates patients and their families about specific medications.
• Responds to emergency situations to assist with medication management (e.g. response to cardiac arrests)
• Provides accurate and timely medication information and or teaching to healthcare professionals or patients.
• Maintains the hospital formulary and acts to limit medication usage to formulary items when appropriate
• Documents all clinical activities and interventions performed. Collects data, maintains logs, records and other documentation as required by the department
• Communicates professional knowledge effectively in both oral and written forms to patients and other health professionals.
• Participates in quality improvement and medication use review activities of the department.
• Organizes, prioritizes, and plans workload within given time constraints. Works cooperatively with fellow pharmacists to oversee and direct the activities of the work area, to assign work to technicians, and to assure that the established department objectives are accomplished
• Reviews restocking automated dispensing cabinets (ADCs) throughout the hospital and resolves any problems.
• Ensures compliance with hazardous waste collection and disposal procedures.
• Maintains proficiency and expertise in area/s of practice through continuous professional development.
• All other job duties as assigned.

Minimum Requirements:

Education:

• Bachelor’s Degree in Pharmacy or a Doctor of Pharmacy Degree

Licensure:

• Active Clinical Pharmacist license in the state of Illinois (IDFPR)

Preferred:

• Training and knowledge of specialty areas (neonatology, critical care, oncology, etc.)
• Completion of a pharmacy residency program or equivalent hospital pharmacy experience

jobs.title: Senior Entomologist
jobs.description:
We are seeking a contract Senior Entomologist to serve as the scientific lead for Colossal Biosciences’ New World Screwworm (NWS; Cochliomyia hominivorax) Biobanking Program, a multi-phase effort to establish a secure, traceable genetic baseline for NWS populations across North and Central America before, during, and after gene drive deployment. This role will design and execute the standardized fitness-validation battery for fresh and cryopreserved (thawed) screwworm cohorts, lead the field collection strategy across active outbreak regions, and oversee live-colony rearing in partnership with COPEG and USDA-APHIS. The Senior Entomologist will act as the central point of scientific accountability for the program — from protocol design and field deployment through data analysis, interpretation, and reporting to federal and partner stakeholders.

This is a 6 month contract position that includes collections trips. You do not need to be based on-site in Dallas but do need to be available for travel.

Key Responsibilities:

• Serve as scientific lead for the NWS Biobanking Program, owning experimental design, protocol standardization, and interpretation of results across Phase 1 (Fitness Validation), Phase 2 (Biobanking), and Phase 3 (Embryology Production) as activated.

• Design, implement, and quality-control the nine-trait fitness battery — mating latency, copulation duration, fecundity, egg hatch rate, larval viability (1st–3rd instar and 3rd instar–pupa), adult eclosion and sex ratio, flight performance, and host-seeking latency — across CF-Gen1, CT-Gen1, CF-Gen2, and CT-Gen2 cohorts.

• Establish and enforce strict standardization of temperature, humidity, photoperiod, age at testing, diet, handling, and observer methods so that cryopreservation-associated fitness effects can be distinguished from normal biological variation.

• Lead statistical analysis of fitness data, including calculation of Hedge’s g effect sizes and percent-difference comparisons relative to the CF-Gen1 baseline, and determine whether observed effects persist, recover, or change across generations.

• Direct the mobile field collection team across priority outbreak regions in Panama, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Honduras, Guatemala, Belize, and southern Mexico, targeting 600–900 individuals from confirmed breeding populations.

• Oversee field collection methods including wound sampling from naturally infested animals, Swormlure-4 baited trapping, rotted-liver bait stations for gravid females, and controlled oviposition on heated substrates to meet live-material targets (2,500+ fertile eggs, 1,200+ larvae, 280+ mated pairs).

• Coordinate with local veterinarians, livestock facilities, COPEG operations, and ongoing eradication efforts to secure site access, maintain cross-border coordination, and ensure enhanced biosecurity protocols in active outbreak zones.

• Oversee live-colony rearing, larval diet preparation, pupation, and eclosion procedures in coordination with COPEG animal care protocols and Arthropod Containment Level 3 (ACL-3) requirements.

• Develop sample chain-of-custody, labeling, metadata, and quality-assurance procedures for live and non-live genetic material entering the biobank in accordance with established biobanking standards.

• Prepare detailed protocols, standard operating procedures, equipment specifications, and training materials for laboratory technicians and field personnel.

• Deliver weekly progress updates and monthly scientific reports to program leadership; prepare data summaries, statistical analyses, and technical narratives for federal and partner stakeholders and regulatory review.

• Provide entomological guidance to embryology, cryopreservation, and cell-culture teams on screwworm developmental biology, reproductive behavior, and host-seeking ecology to support colony reconstitution and restoration success metrics.

• Support post-intervention monitoring design, including documentation of genetic bottlenecks, founder effects, and population dynamics during range expansion.

• Contribute to peer-reviewed publications, technical reports, and presentations that communicate program findings to the scientific and regulatory communities.

Required Skills and Abilities:

• Deep expertise in insect behavioral ecology, host selection, and developmental biology, with demonstrated ability to design and run rigorous laboratory behavioral and life-history assays.

• Strong foundation in experimental design and applied statistics, including effect-size analysis, power analysis, and interpretation of variance in behavioral and reproductive traits.

• Hands-on experience with insect field sampling and monitoring methods, including baited and pheromone trapping, sentinel or bait-station collection, and standardized arthropod survey techniques.

• Experience establishing and maintaining live insect colonies under controlled environmental conditions, including diet formulation and rearing standardization.

• Proven ability to lead interdisciplinary research teams and to coordinate across scientific, operations, and external partner organizations.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to author protocols, technical reports, and peer-reviewed manuscripts and to present findings to executive and government stakeholders.

• Working knowledge of biosafety, containment, and animal-care compliance requirements for arthropod research facilities.

• Willingness and ability to travel to and work in field settings across Central America and southern Mexico, including active livestock outbreak zones.

Preferred Skills and Certifications:

• Direct experience with Diptera, particularly Calliphoridae or other myiasis-causing or livestock-pest flies; familiarity with Cochliomyia hominivorax biology, the Sterile Insect Technique, and COPEG operations strongly preferred.

• Prior research experience with USDA-ARS, USDA-APHIS, or comparable federal or international agricultural research programs.

• Background in biological control, beneficial insect introduction, or area-wide integrated pest management programs.

• Familiarity with cryopreservation, biobanking, or genetic resource preservation programs for insects or other invertebrates.

• Experience working under Arthropod Containment Level 2 or 3 (ACL-2/ACL-3) conditions or with USDA-APHIS permitting.

• Proficiency in statistical software (R, SAS, or similar) and data management platforms for large behavioral datasets.

• Spanish language proficiency a plus.

• Record of peer-reviewed publications in entomology, behavioral ecology, or related fields.

Education and Experience:

• Ph.D. in Entomology, Behavioral Ecology, or a closely related field required; emphasis in experimental statistics or ecological biochemistry a plus.

• 15 or more years of progressive research experience in entomology or insect ecology, with a substantial portion in a lead scientist or principal investigator role.

• Demonstrated track record of leading multi-year, multi-site research programs from design through publication.

• Experience in academic, federal, or industry research environments; adjunct or teaching experience in entomology or wildlife ecology a plus.

• Proven ability to mentor and supervise technicians, students, and early-career scientists.

What Colossal Offers Full-Time Employees:

• Medical, dental, and vision coverage

• Excellent paid time off and company holidays so you can rest and recharge

• Flexible spending accounts (FSA)

• Company matched 401k retirement plan

• Paid parental leave at 100% salary for up to 12 weeks

• Education reimbursement

• An opportunity to help us return the Earth to a healthier state

The team at Colossal is committed, colorful, passionate, intelligent, collaborative, creative, experienced, scientific and world-class. That sounds like a lot to fit into one building. That’s why we are spread out in several locations that include laboratories, test facilities, academic institutions, libraries and offices.

Through it all, however, we maintain a culture of positivity, hope, happiness and belief that we’re doing something big. Something Colossal.

Colossal is proud to be an equal employment opportunity workplace. We welcome people from all backgrounds as well as celebrate and support diversity. We are committed to providing an inclusive environment of mutual respect that is free from discrimination and harassment so everyone can thrive.

EEO is the Law

Search Firm Representatives: Colossal does not accept unsolicited assistance from search firms. No fees will be paid for a hired candidate where no pre-existing agreement is in place. We handle most recruitment in-house.

• 100 Best Places to Work in Dallas, TX (All Size Employers) in 2024, 2025, and 2026.
