jobs.title: Principal Product Marketing Manager -  Go-To-Market
jobs.description:
Who we are
Mindtickle is the leading AI-powered revenue enablement platform, helping sales teams learn faster, practice smarter, and perform at their best. We bring together onboarding, training, coaching, content, digital sales rooms, conversation intelligence, and AI role-plays into one platform so revenue teams have everything they need to build winning sellers.
Global companies, like Fortune 500 organizations, trust Mindtickle to support their revenue teams. Customers and industry analysts have also recognized us. G2 has ranked us the #1 Sales Training & Onboarding platform for 28 consecutive quarters, and Forrester has recognized Mindtickle as a Leader in revenue enablement. Mindtickle was also recognized as AI-Based Sales Solution of the Year by the 2025 AI Breakthrough Awards and has received Stevie Awards for Technology Innovation and Customer Support Excellence.
At Mindtickle, we're helping companies create high-performing revenue teams, and we're looking for people who want to help shape what's next.


About the role
Mindtickle is moving from a market perception as a sales training and enablement platform to recognition as the AI-native revenue enablement platform, powered by ElevateOS. The product work is underway. The harder problem is market meaning: whether the market understands why any of this matters, why it matters now, and why Mindtickle is the company that should own it.
You will own the answer. Specifically, you own the category narrative behind Mindtickle and ElevateOS and the translation of that narrative into value that each buyer recognises as their own problem. The narrative cannot be a list of agentic capabilities. AI Roleplay, AI Tutor, Deal Guide, Buyer Copilot, Knowledge Copilot and Call AI have to ladder into a single category idea: Mindtickle, powered by ElevateOS helps revenue teams win every moment that matters by turning readiness into live execution. Your job is to make that idea true, specific, provable and repeatable, and then to make it show up identically on the website, in the sales deck, in the demo, in the analyst briefing and in the board narrative.
This is a company-level clarity role. You will work directly with the CEO, the co-founders, Product, Sales, Solution Consulting, Customer Success and Analyst Relations. It is also a hands-on role: you will personally write the positioning, the message architecture and the persona narratives that the rest of the company draws from.
Your measure of success is simple: does the market repeat it? Can Sales say it in one sentence without reading a slide? Do customers hear a business argument rather than AI buzzwording? Can analysts place Mindtickle in a category and describe how it differs? Does the demo make the positioning tangible? And do deals move, save and expand because of the story rather than in spite of it?
What you will own:
1 - The category narrative behind ElevateOS
Build and maintain the answer to why the world needs ElevateOS now. Ladder the portfolio of agentic capabilities into one category idea instead of a portfolio tour. Hold the line on the four questions the market will ask in sequence: why change, why now, why Mindtickle, why not the alternatives. The narrative you write is the one the company defends in front of analysts, boards, and CROs, so it has to survive scrutiny from people who are paid to be skeptical.
2- The message architecture, held as one source of truth
Codify master positioning, the differentiation argument, the claim set and the proof each claim rests on. Every downstream artefact draws from this document rather than from a fresh interpretation. You version it as the platform and the market move, you decide what enters and what is retired, and you are the person who says a piece of language is off-architecture. One message architecture feeding many artefacts is the mechanism that stops the company from producing many disconnected deliverables.
3- The buyer translation layer
Convert the platform story into a specific value story for each buyer: revenue leaders who own win rate, ramp time and forecast confidence; enablement leaders moving from programmatic enablement to always-on agentic enablement; frontline managers who need to coach with evidence rather than anecdotes; sellers who need guidance in the flow of work, before the call and during the deal; buyers who experience the engagement; and CIO and RevOps stakeholders who care about interoperability, governance, integrations and enterprise readiness. Each persona gets pain, trigger, value proposition, proof and objection handling. The bar is that an AE can take it into a live enterprise conversation without translating it first.
4- Buyer pain as the default language for every capability
Express each capability through the business problem it solves, the impact it creates and the evidence behind it. "Deal Guide gives sellers AI recommendations" fails the bar. "Deal Guide helps managers and sellers identify deal risk early by connecting Salesforce context, buyer questions, stakeholder gaps, competitive intelligence and win-loss patterns into one execution guide" passes it. Apply the same test to every claim: does the claim communicate differentiation, or does it prompt a follow-up question?
5- The differentiation argument against alternative architectures
Own why ElevateOS is architecturally different from conversation intelligence tools, content and enablement platforms, LMS incumbents, CRM add-ons and single-purpose AI agents. The argument is structural: others attach AI to content, calls or CRM records, while Mindtickle connects readiness, seller behaviour, buyer engagement and deal execution in one system. Competitive Intelligence owns the tactical layer of battlecards, landmines and counters. You own the architectural argument those tactics are built on, and you own keeping it honest as competitors ship.
6- One voice across every surface
Website, sales deck, customer deck, demo narrative, analyst pitch, webinar, executive and board narrative should be recognisably the same story told at different lengths. Drift is the normal state of a fast-moving company, so treat detection and correction as standing work rather than a project. You will audit surfaces, name where the story has fragmented, and drive the fix with the owner of that surface.
7-The language quality bar
Decide what the market should remember about Mindtickle and ElevateOS, in a handful of phrases, and then defend that simplicity against the pull toward more slides, more words and more qualifiers. Polished and verbose is a failure state. The output you are after is language that a seller, a customer, an analyst and a board member can each repeat accurately from memory.
8-Category framing for analyst relations and launches
Feed the category thesis and differentiation into analyst briefing cycles and launch moments, leading with the market problem before the product. Analyst Relations owns coverage, relationships and evaluation cycles. Launch commercialisation owns the launch operating system and whether a given launch lands. You own the positioning both of them build on, and you stay close enough to both to know when the story needs to change rather than the execution.
9- Proximity to revenue reality
Positioning built from internal product assumptions decays quickly. Work from win-loss patterns, live sales calls, Solution Consulting demo friction, renewal and expansion objections, and analyst perception gaps. Test messages in real conversations rather than in review meetings. Where the field keeps hitting the same objection, that is a positioning defect, and it is yours to fix. Feed differentiation gaps back into roadmap prioritisation so Product hears the market argument, not only the feature request.
How this role works across the organization.
Function You own:
Head of Product Marketing
PMM strategy, priorities, the org-level quality bar
You author the category narrative and message architecture, the rest of PMM draws from
Launch commercialisation
The launch operating system, the integrated launch motion, and whether a launch lands
You own the positioning of each launch narrative ladder. Shared ground: the launch narrative itself. You supply the architecture and the differentiation argument, they own the market moment and the field motion. Neither of you ships a launch story that the other has not seen
Field product marketing and competitive
Signal from live deals, competitors, and win-loss; the tactical battlecard layer
You own the architectural differentiation argument and convert the field signal into positioning and objection-handling changes. Shared ground: competitive messaging, where they own what a rep says in the room and you own why the claim is true
Customer marketing
The proof engine, customer evidence, references, and voice of customer
You own which claims require proof and which proof points carry the differentiation argument. Shared ground: claim-to-evidence matching, run as a standing review rather than an ad hoc request
Analyst relations
Analyst coverage, briefing calendar, evaluation cycles
You own the category thesis, differentiation and proof logic the analyst story rests on
Product management
Product strategy, roadmap, usage outcomes
You bring market perception and differentiation gaps into roadmap prioritization
Sales and Solution Consulting
Customer conversations, technical demo environments, and execution
You own the source narrative and the story that the demo must prove. Shared ground: demo storytelling standards, held jointly with launch commercialization
Demand generation and web
Campaign and site execution
You own the story, the site and campaigns express, and the standard they are held to
What success looks like in your first year
What you are accountable for
The company is sharper about what ElevateOS is. There is a clear market thesis, written down, and Product, Sales, CS, Analyst Relations, web, and the executive team works from it rather than around it.
The category language starts coming back to you. Analysts, customers, and competitors begin using the framing you introduced. This is the highest bar in the role and the one worth aiming at.
Every persona has a specific story. Pain, trigger, value proposition, proof, and objection handling exist for CRO, enablement leader, frontline manager, seller, buyer, and technical buyer, and Sales uses them directly in enterprise conversations.
No capability is described in capability language. Each product is expressed through buyer pain, business impact, and evidence.
The surfaces agree. Website, decks, demo, webinar, analyst pitch, and board narrative reinforce one story, and drift is caught in weeks rather than quarters.
The language is simple enough for travel. A handful of phrases about ElevateOS are repeatable by sellers, customers, analysts, and board members without a slide in front of them.
Where you contribute to outcomes that others own
Demos make the positioning believable. You own the story the demo must prove, and you push until the demo carries a business argument rather than a feature sequence.
Launches compound the category story. Each launch strengthens the ElevateOS thesis rather than adding an unconnected message.
Competitive displacement gets easier. The architectural argument gives Field PMM and Sales something durable to build traps and counters on.
Analysts can place us. Category thesis, differentiation, and proof are clear enough that analyst placement stops being a reactive scramble.
PMM work shows up in revenue outcomes. Positioning changes are traceable to competitive wins, renewals saved, and expansion conversations opened.
What you bring:
8+ years in product marketing or a closely adjacent discipline, preferably enterprise B2B SaaS, with a track record of operating as a senior individual contributor who owns outcomes end to end.
Category and narrative depth. Demonstrated ability to build positioning and a message architecture from the market problem upward, and to hold a company to one consistent story across every surface over time.
Fluency across very different buyers. You can express the same platform in the language of a CRO, an enablement leader, a frontline manager, a seller and a RevOps or IT stakeholder, grounded in the pain and the business impact each of them owns.
Exceptional written communication. High standards for precision, and the judgement to know when a claim is sharp enough to differentiate and when it is still a placeholder.
Architectural instincts about competition. You can explain why a competitor's approach is structurally limited, and you keep that argument current as they ship.
Cross-functional influence without authority. You can align Product, Sales, Solution Consulting, Customer Success, Marketing, and leadership in a matrixed, fast-moving environment.
High agency in a flat organization. This is a senior IC role inside a team going through a transformation. You set direction, move without waiting for instructions, and are accountable for the outcome rather than the activity. You can do the work yourself at an expert level and design the system that scales it.
Maker-checker discipline with AI. You treat AI as the maker for research, synthesis, and repeatable production, and yourself as the checker for positioning judgment and quality. You know which decisions a system can carry out and which require a human.
Comfort with ambiguity and pace. A self-starter who treats raw, fast iteration as a strength.
Experience in AI, agentic systems, revenue technology, enablement, or adjacent categories is particularly valuable.
How you operate
You hold a point of view. You come with a position, you argue it with evidence, and you change it when the field or the market tells you something better.
You start from the buyer. Product capability is where the conversation ends, not where it starts.
You simplify. You turn a sophisticated agentic platform into language that a CRO, a seller, or a customer can repeat.
You look for evidence. A claim without proof is a liability, and you would rather remove it than defend it.
You use AI as leverage. Aggressively for research, synthesis, and first-pass creation, deliberately not for the judgment calls.
You know the difference between complete and commercially excellent. Polished is not the same as sharp.
The profile we are looking for is not a messaging writer who packages product updates. Not a strategist who stops at the framework. A senior product marketer who can define what category Mindtickle is playing in, prove it, translate it for six different buyers, and hold an entire company to one story while the product and the market are both still moving. The question this person naturally asks: "What does the market need to believe for ElevateOS to matter, and is our story good enough to make them believe it?"

jobs.title: Accounts Assistant
jobs.description:

The Bayview Geographe Resort is an unbranded property Managed by Accor.

Must be willing to undergo a police check.

jobs.title: Team Leader, SRE
jobs.description:
About Remote

Remote is solving modern organizations’ biggest challenge – navigating global employment compliantly with ease. We make it possible for businesses of all sizes to recruit, pay, and manage international teams. With our core values at heart and future focused work culture, our team works tirelessly on ambitious problems, asynchronously, around the world. You can find Remoters working from 6 different continents (Antarctica left to go!) and all of our positions are fully remote.

With Innovation as one of the core values, we have built Automation and AI capabilities into the requirements for every role.

We encourage every member of the Remote team to bring their talents, experiences and culture to the table to help us build the best-in-class HR platform.

If you are energetic, curious, motivated and ambitious, be part of our world. Apply now and define the future of work!

What this job can offer you

Remote's SRE team exists so that our engineers can move quickly and our customers get a product that stays up. The team owns Kubernetes, AWS, PostgreSQL, CI infrastructure, our observability stack and the reliability practices that sits on top of all of it.

We are looking for a Team Leader to run that team. This is a 60% IC, 40% leadership role. You will own the career development of your reports, steer the teams focus using judgment against the company goals, and you will be the spokesperson for the team across engineering. You will also stay close enough to the technical work to set direction with credibility and to know when something is going wrong before it is escalated to you.

Reliability practice at Remote is maturing rather than mature. Our SLO framework is live on its first few teams and needs to reach the rest, there is real work to do on how we balance operational load against project delivery. If you want a team where the foundations are in place and the interesting problems are still open, this is that team.

What you bring

People leadership

• You have led an SRE, infrastructure or platform engineering team, and you have owned your reports' growth, performance and career progression rather than just their sprints.

• You coach both craft and the soft skills, you can point to people who grew because of it.

• You handle underperformance directly and early, with clarity and empathy.

• You have hired engineers, and you can tell the difference between a good interview and a good engineer.

• You read team dynamics well and you resolve conflict rather than routing around it.

• You have a natural talent fostering commitment to the goals of the company.

Technical depth

• A hands-on background in site reliability, DevOps or cloud infrastructure engineering, deep enough that you can review your team's work, challenge a design and be taken seriously in an incident.

• Kubernetes in production, including the operational reality of it rather than the happy path.

• AWS at meaningful scale.

• Hands on AI building, enablement, scaling AI infrastructure.

• Solid o11y practices and principles,

• Infrastructure as code with Terraform.

• CI/CD systems such as GitLab CI, GitHub Actions or Jenkins.

• Docker and shell scripting.

• You have run a reliability practice: incident response, on-call, SLOs and error budgets, and the discipline of turning incidents into changes that stick.

• Understanding and history of working in regulated environments.

Ways of working

• You prioritise exceptionally well when operational load and project work compete, and you protect your team's focus without dropping the operational commitment.

• You write clearly. Remote is fully distributed and async, so most of your leadership will happen in writing.

• You build relationships across teams. A lot of SRE's value comes from being the team others bring problems to early.

Nice to have

• Working knowledge of a backend language, ideally Elixir, or otherwise Java, Clojure, Node.js, Python or similar.

• Depth in modern observability: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, and tools such as Honeycomb.

• Database operations experience, particularly PostgreSQL or Aurora performance, connection pool health and query tuning.

• Running and configuring Linux systems outside a cloud environment.

• Security capability from both a defensive and an offensive standpoint.

• Cloud cost management and FinOps.

• Experience growing a team from a small base, including building the hiring bar as you go.

Key Responsibilities

Your people

• The full career lifecycle of your reports: onboarding, feedback, performance assessment, progression and hiring.

• Team health, dynamics and the retrospective habit that keeps them honest.

• Being the team's spokesperson to the rest of engineering and to senior leadership.

Delivery

• The SRE goals: what the team commits to, in what order, and why.

• The support rotation and on-call model.

The platform

• Remote's core infrastructure: Kubernetes, AWS, PostgreSQL, DNS and TLS, CI infrastructure.

• The reliability practice: SLOs, error budgets, incident response and the observability stack.

• The partnership with our Security team on threats, patching and infrastructure controls, including our audit and compliance obligations.

• The vendor relationships that sit behind the platform, including renewals and commercial conversations with support from your Director.

Practicals

• You will report to: Director of Engineering, Platform

• Team: Site Reliability Engineering, part of Platform Engineering

• Direct reports: 4

• Location: Anywhere in the world. Our current coverage is strongest in EMEA and APAC, so candidates who overlap with either, or who can help us close the Americas gap, are especially welcome.

• Start date: As soon as possible

Application process

• Interview with recruiter

• Interview with hiring manager

• Scenario interview with a peer team leader

• Executive interview

• Bar Raiser interview

• Offer + Prior employment verification check

#LI-DNP

Remote's Total Rewards philosophy is to ensure fair, unbiased compensation and fair equity pay along with competitive benefits in all locations in which we operate. We do not agree to or encourage cheap-labor practices and therefore we ensure to pay above in-location rates. We hope to inspire other companies to support global talent-hiring and bring local wealth to developing countries.

At first glance our salary bands seem quite wide - here is some context. At Remote we have international operations and a globally distributed workforce.  We use geo ranges to consider geographic pay differentials as part of our global compensation strategy to remain competitive in various markets while we hiring globally.

Our salary ranges are determined by role, level and location, and our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay for the successful candidate in this role is dependent upon many factors such as location, transferable or job-related skills, work experience, relevant training, business needs, and market demands. The base salary range may be subject to change.

At Remote, we foster internal mobility as a key element of our culture of employee growth and development, supported by a compensation philosophy that guarantees pay equity and fairness. Therefore, all compensation changes associated with an internal move will be reviewed by the Total Rewards & People Enablement team on a case by case basis.

The annual salary range for this full-time position is

$75,450—$169,700 USD

Benefits

Our full benefits & perks are explained in our handbook at remote.com/r/benefits. As a global company, each country works differently, but some benefits/perks are for all Remoters:

• work from anywhere

• flexible paid time off

• flexible working hours (we are async)

• 16 weeks paid parental leave

• mental health support services

• stock options

• learning budget

• home office budget & IT equipment

• budget for local in-person social events or co-working spaces

How you’ll plan your day (and life)

We work async at Remote which means you can plan your schedule around your life (and not around meetings). Read more at remote.com/async.

You will be empowered to take ownership and be proactive. When in doubt you will default to action instead of waiting. Your life-work balance is important and you will be encouraged to put yourself and your family first, and fit work around your needs.

If that sounds like something you want, apply now!

How to apply

• Please fill out the form below and upload your CV with a PDF format.

• We kindly ask you to submit your application and CV in English, as this is the standardised language we use here at Remote.

• If you don’t have an up to date CV but you are still interested in talking to us, please feel free to add a copy of your LinkedIn profile instead.

We will ask you to voluntarily tell us your pronouns at interview stage, and you will have the option to answer our anonymous demographic questionnaire when you apply below. As an equal employment opportunity employer it’s important to us that our workforce reflects people of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences and this data will help us to stay accountable. We thank you for providing this data, if you chose to.

Please note we accept applications on an ongoing basis.

jobs.title: 002-09-2026 SUPERVISEUR TERRAIN & CONTRÔLEUR DE RISQUE / BUKAVU et KINSHASA
jobs.description:
GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026.

Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit!

• Background :

GiveDirectly (GD) vise à remodeler les dons internationaux - et des millions de vies - en fournissant des subventions en espèces directement aux plus pauvres du monde. The Brookings Institution estime que 70 milliards de dollars de transferts en espèces seraient nécessaires pour éliminer le fossé de la pauvreté ; le secteur de l'aide dépense actuellement 135 milliards de dollars par an, dont une grande partie pour des interventions non fondées sur des données probantes. GiveDirectly veut changer cela, en faisant des transferts d'argent liquide une référence pour l'aide étrangère - comme le fonds indiciel est une référence pour l'industrie financière - et en accélérant ainsi la fin de l'extrême pauvreté.

GD a levé plus de 700 millions de dollars depuis son lancement en 2011, distribué de l'argent à plus d'un million de personnes et ouvert des bureaux dans 10 pays. Nous avons également soutenu des recherches expérimentales à grande échelle qui indiquent un fort impact de nos programmes sur les bénéficiaires. En conséquence, GD a été reconnue comme l'une des organisations à but non lucratif les plus innovantes par Fast Company, tandis que le mouvement croissant des transferts d'argent liquide (et le rôle de premier plan joué par la GD dans ce cadre) a fait l'objet d'un article dans le magazine New York Times Magazine, This American Life, Foreign Affairs, et The Economist.

GiveDirectly offre la possibilité de travailler avec des personnes originaires de 21 pays différents et parlant 69 langues différentes. Nous travaillons activement à la mise en place d'un environnement équitable et inclusif pour tous les membres de l'équipe, et notre personnel apporte des perspectives et des expériences diverses à notre organisation. Dans nos bureaux du monde entier, notre culture est franche, analytique, non hiérarchique et rapide. Nous valorisons les capacités, l'adaptabilité et la volonté d'apprendre.

À propos de GiveDirectly en RD Congo :

GiveDirectly RDC a été créé en 2018 afin de permettre des transferts monétaires aux populations pauvres et rurales via les téléphones portables, afin de promouvoir la sécurité alimentaire, la réduction de la pauvreté et l’inclusion financière. Nous souhaitions démontrer la faisabilité opérationnelle et la rentabilité du transfert d’importants volumes monétaires sous forme numérique dans l’un des pays les moins développés du monde. Depuis sa création, il y a quatre ans, GiveDirectly RDC a utilisé les téléphones mobiles pour transférer plus de 14 millions de dollars à plus de 65 000 bénéficiaires dans quatre provinces : Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Ituri et Kinshasa. Les activités de GiveDirectly en RDC se sont développées de manière à inclure, notamment : des preuves de concept convaincantes des transferts d’argent liquide basés sur les téléphones portables ; la mise en œuvre de technologies innovantes de ciblage des populations urbaines défavorisées de Kinshasa, en collaboration avec l’agence de protection sociale de la RDC, le Fonds Social de la RDC ; la livraison d’argent liquide sans contact aux bénéficiaires de Beni et Bunia affectés par les conséquences économiques de la COVID-19. Vous rejoindrez Give Directly RDC à un moment passionnant de son histoire, alors que nous mettons en place et espérons lancer plusieurs nouveaux programmes et renforcer notre partenariat avec le gouvernement de la RDC.

SUPERVISEUR TERRAIN & CONTROLEUR DE RISQUE

Taches et Responsabilitesa propos du rôle

Le Superviseur terrain & Contrôleur de risque, sur le terrain joue un rôle essentiel pour garantir que GiveDirectly offre un service d'excellence aux donateurs et aux bénéficiaires. Véritable interlocuteur/trice privilégié(e) de l'organisation sur le terrain, il/elle sera chargé(e) de synthétiser régulièrement les informations relatives aux performances de l'équipe, ainsi qu'aux réussites et aux difficultés rencontrées.

Ils travailleront en toute indépendance et séparément des autres équipes du programme. Ils seront totalement isolés des autres équipes de terrain.

Le Superviseur terrain & Contrôleur de risque dirigera une équipe d'audit des programmes qui surveillera, détectera et résoudra les risques liés aux programmes, tels que la fraude et les violations des règles de sécurité, grâce à divers flux de travail, y compris des enquêtes sur le terrain.Ils seront responsables de l'ensemble du processus d'audit du programme, notamment du suivi des performances de leurs équipes, de l'atteinte des objectifs en matière d'enquêtes et de résolution de cas, de la mise en place d'une culture de mentorat et de développement professionnel, du suivi des tendances en matière de risques liés aux projets et de l'identification des opportunités d'atténuation des risques et d'amélioration des processus.

Ce poste exigera un jugement sûr sur les questions et les défis opérationnels, de solides compétences en communication et en relations interpersonnelles, une gestion exceptionnelle du personnel et un engagement ferme envers les valeurs, la mission et le modèle de GiveDirectly. Ce poste nécessitera des déplacements réguliers sur les lieux de travail.

L'équipe d'audit interne est strictement anonyme. De ce fait, ses communications et correspondances sont protégées et inaccessibles à l'équipe des programmes de GiveDirectly. Le responsable de l'audit interne bénéficie également d'une protection stricte et encadre une équipe anonyme dont les communications sont elles aussi protégées. En rejoignant l'équipe d'audit interne, vous vous engagez à exercer vos fonctions avec le plus haut degré de confidentialité et d'anonymat.

Fonctions et responsabilités
Conception de projet - prévention et atténuation des risques (25%)

• Diriger le processus de consultation communautaire avant le lancement des projets et soumettre un rapport complet au chef de projet de l'IA

• Collaborer avec le chef de projet en matière d'assurance de l'information afin de concevoir des registres des risques au niveau du pays et du projet.

• Contrôles de qualité des données des partenaires principaux pour garantir l'exactitude des données soumises

• Examiner les outils de mise en œuvre pour assurer la détection, la prévention et l'atténuation adéquates des risques

surveillance des risques axée sur les systèmes (50%)

• Collaborer avec le chef de projet IA pour définir et examiner les classifications des risques en fonction des projets et du pays.

• Prendre l'initiative d'enquêter sur les cas présumés de fraude et d'abus, notamment en communiquant les informations pertinentes au responsable du programme pour la remontée d'informations et/ou la résolution nécessaires.

• S'assurer que les dossiers et les questions en cours d'instruction soient résolus dans les délais impartis.

• Créer et tenir à jour des rapports et des tableaux de bord reflétant les performances de l'équipe par rapport à l'objectif fixé.

• Diriger l'équipe chargée d'effectuer un suivi régulier des renseignements sur la fraude au sein de la communauté tout au long du cycle de projet

• Évaluer les tendances et les causes sous-jacentes des risques liés aux programmes de transfert monétaire inconditionnel de GiveDirectly

• Diriger l'équipe d'audit des programmes internes dans la détection des risques tels que les atteintes à la sécurité, la fraude, les abus et les conflits d'intérêts non déclarés ; en assurant la confidentialité des rapports, la détection proactive, les enquêtes approfondies et la gestion des cas de risques chaque fois qu'ils surviennent.

• Assurer la direction de l'examen et du contrôle ponctuel de la qualité des données de l'équipe du programme par rapport aux normes de qualité des données GD établies et signaler tout cas d'incohérence.

Collaborer avec les autres équipes de données mondiales de GD pour développer les outils d'enquête nécessaires à l'exécution de la fonction.

• Gestion d'équipe (15%)

• Élaborer et gérer les plans de travail d'équipe pour tous les projets

• Effectuer des contrôles de qualité de l'équipe par le biais d'observations sur le terrain et d'examens des données des enquêtes et des dossiers de l'équipe.

• Adopter un comportement éthique exemplaire qui encourage l'équipe à respecter les politiques de GD et à signaler tout manquement à la déontologie au sein du personnel, des partenaires, de la communauté et parmi les bénéficiaires de GD.

jobs.title: Solution Consulting Manager
jobs.description:
The Role:

This is a player-manager role. Roughly 70% of your time goes to building and running the team; the remaining 30% is yours to own a focused set of strategic deals in the region. As the Solution Consulting Manager in the Americas, you will play a pivotal leadership role at the intersection of commercial strategy, technical excellence, and customer impact. You will build and lead Elliptic's Solution Consulting function across the Americas. You’ll drive technical and commercial excellence across the region, champion value-based and consultative selling, and work closely with regional VPs to support all aspects of our customer lifecycle. In addition, you will collaborate deeply with Engineering and Product Marketing to unify Elliptic’s GTM strategy and accelerate solution innovation.

You’ll shape our regional approach to Enterprise strategy, mentor your teams in best practices, and ensure Elliptic’s solutions deliver measurable value for enterprise clients. Your ability to communicate complex ideas in commercial terms, coach technical talent, and align cross-functional regional efforts will be key to success in this client-facing, high-impact role.

Key Responsibilities:

 - Own a focused set of strategic deals in the region alongside your management responsibilities.

 - Build, recruit, and coach a high-performing team of Solution Consultants in key Americas, fostering a collaborative and feedback-driven culture.

 - Develop best practices in consultative selling -  discovery, technical demonstration, value-based selling, solution architecture, and POC/pilot delivery for enterprise clients.

 - Partner with Engineering and Product Marketing on roadmap planning, product releases, technical messaging, and customer feedback loops.

 - Guide and support complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise sales opportunities, mapping workflows, proving value, and designing solution integration plans with measurable impact.

 - Own the solution consultant processes, enablement plans, and continuously optimise with automation, AI, and modern productivity tools.

 - Interface closely with Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Product, GPRG and SME’s groups to upskill our solution consultant team to articulate Elliptic’s technical value in the context of regulatory, compliance, and evolving client needs.

 - Ensure consistency of technical product feedback, demo environments, regional regulatory awareness, and sales excellence across the teams.

 - Drive adoption of Elliptic’s solutions across diverse enterprise architectures, address integration challenges, and ensure customer success.


YOU MUST HAVE:

 - Over 5 years of experience leading pre-sales and Solutions Consulting teams in B2B SaaS enterprise software companies.

 
 


REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 - Blockchain analytics, Digital Assets or Crypto Compliance.

 - Demonstrable experience in enterprise SaaS solution consulting, sales engineering, or pre-sales roles in Enterprise SaaS B2B companies

 - Proven track record of building, leading, and scaling Solution Consulting teams of approximately 10 people.

 - Deep understanding of value-based and consultative selling methodologies within complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise sales cycles.

 - Demonstrable experience working closely with Engineering and Product Marketing to shape product roadmap, technical messaging, and GTM strategies.

 - Strong technical fluency, including hands-on experience with APIs, integration workflows, cloud environments, and enterprise architecture.

 - Experience designing and leading tailored product demos, pilots, and POC engagements that highlight commercial value and technical feasibility.

 - Proven ability to manage advanced stakeholder relationships across sales, research, policy, and strategic partner teams.

 - Track record of driving continuous improvement through team development, data analytics, automation, and modern productivity tools

 - A track record of automating internal processes using AI, scripting, or innovative tools to improve efficiency and consistency.



Key Performance Indicators :

 - Technical Win Rate: Percentage of qualified opportunities where the Solution Consulting team successfully achieved a technical win, reflecting solution validation by the customer.

 - PoV/PoC Conversion Rate: Rate at which proof-of-value or proof-of-concept engagements convert into closed-won deals, especially within strategic or enterprise segments.

 - Sales Cycle Impact: Reduction in average sales cycle duration attributed to Solution Consulting's involvement in discovery, solution design, and stakeholder alignment.

 - Ramp Time to Productivity: Time taken for new Solution Consultants to become fully effective, measured through client engagement readiness, demo delivery, and value articulation.

 - Demo Quality and Utilisation: Consistency, availability, and adoption of demo environments and technical storytelling assets, based on internal feedback and usage metrics.

 - Team Utilisation & Coverage: Balanced distribution of SC team bandwidth across priority accounts and regions, ensuring responsiveness without resource overextension.

 - Cross-Functional Engagement: Depth and quality of collaboration with Product, Sales, and Marketing teams, including contributions to roadmap feedback, content creation, and go-to-market alignment.



Preferred

 - Familiarity with blockchain analytics tools, crypto transaction tracing, or on-chain intelligence

 - Knowledge and experience in compliance, financial crime, and fintech.

 - Adopter of new technologies and use of AI-enhanced productivity apps, Zapier, Notion, and data visualisation tools.

 - Experience with coding or scripting (e.g., Python, SQL, JavaScript) for tasks such as data manipulation, API testing, or light prototyping.



How we work:

 - Hybrid working: The option to work from almost anywhere for up to 90 days per year.

 - Remote Work Budget: $650 budget to set up your home office space.

Learning & Development:

 - L&D Budget: $1,000 annual Learning & Development budget to use on anything (agreed with your manager) that contributes to your growth and development.

Vacation / Leave:

 - Holidays: 25 days of annual leave + US Public Holidays.

 - Birthday Leave: An extra day off for your birthday.

 - Enhanced Parental Leave: We provide eligible employees, regardless of gender or whether they become a parent by birth or adoption, 16 weeks fully-paid leave.

Benefits:

 - Healthcare: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage through a range of providers (including Tufts, Kaiser, Aetna, UHC, and Blue Shield of CA) with generous premium contributions for you and your dependents.

 - 401k: Company match included.

 - Mental Health: Full access to Spill mental health support.

jobs.title: Senior Specialist I, Logistics
jobs.description:
Step into a career with ASM, where cutting edge technology meets collaborative culture. ​

For over 55 years ASM has been ahead of what’s next, at the forefront of innovation and what’s technologically possible. With more than 4,500 ASMers representing 70 nationalities, our people and our advanced semiconductor devices are playing a crucial role in trends such as 5G, cloud computing, AI, and autonomous driving.  But we’re more than just a tech company. We value diversity, inclusion and sustainability as we strive to make a positive impact on the world.  Our development programs help support your growth, shaping your future and pushing the boundaries of innovation to unleash potential.

Position Summary

The Logistics Specialist is responsible for the day‑to‑day execution and oversight of domestic and international logistics operations, ensuring on‑time delivery, cost efficiency, regulatory compliance, and high customer satisfaction. This role partners closely with 3PL providers, carriers, and cross‑functional internal teams to support effective logistics execution.

The position requires deep, hands‑on knowledge of warehouse operations, including dock, stockroom, and floor execution, combined with strong data analytics capabilities to monitor performance, identify trends, and drive productivity, throughput, and inventory accuracy improvements. This role also supports the New Product Introduction (NPI) organization by enabling R&D activities through data‑driven logistics planning, timely material movement, and accurate inventory execution.

As part of the Americas Logistics organization, this role plays a critical part in maintaining material flow, inventory integrity, and overall operational excellence.

Key Responsibilities

• Oversee daily warehouse and distribution operations, including inbound receiving, put‑away, storage, picking, packing, staging, shipping, and return to stock (RTS) logistics.

• Maintain strong, routine presence and visibility on the warehouse floor, stockrooms, and dock areas to ensure safe, efficient, and compliant material movement.

• Understand and manage key warehouse productivity drivers, including labor utilization, throughput, space optimization, inventory accuracy, dock‑to‑stock cycle time, and shipment velocity.

• Monitor and analyze warehouse and logistics performance using operational data, dashboards, and reports to identify trends, bottlenecks, and opportunities for improvement.

• Apply data analytics to drive decisions related to productivity, capacity planning, inventory accuracy, transportation performance, and cost control.

• Develop and support performance metrics and KPIs (e.g., pick rates, dock turns, inventory accuracy, on‑time shipment performance) and use data to drive corrective actions.

• Identify root causes of inefficiencies in warehouse, stockroom, and dock operations and lead process improvements to increase efficiency and consistency.

• Ensure accurate and timely SAP transactions for all warehouse and logistics activities, including goods receipt, goods issue, stock transfers, returns, and inventory adjustments.

• Maintain high levels of inventory accuracy through disciplined system transactions, cycle counts, and physical inventory controls.

• Manage and support U.S. import and export operations in compliance with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and other applicable regulations.

• Coordinate with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and carriers to ensure accurate documentation, classification, valuation, and timely clearance of U.S. imports and exports.

• Collaborate closely with 3PL providers, carriers, and internal teams to align warehouse execution, transportation schedules, and dock operations.

• Partner with Manufacturing, Production Planning, Quality, Purchasing, and Trade Compliance teams to resolve material flow and compliance issues.

• Review and audit freight, handling, and accessorial costs using data‑driven analysis to identify cost reduction opportunities.

• Respond proactively to internal and external customer inquiries and escalations related to warehouse execution, shipment status, and delivery performance.

• Participate in operational reviews, scorecards, monthly business reviews (MBRs) and continuous improvement initiatives with warehouse service providers and logistics partners.

• Perform other job‑related duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering or equivalent related experience

• 7+ years of experience in domestic and international Logistics, Transportation, or Supply Chain Management for the capital equipment industry, preferably semiconductor or hi-tech manufacturing environment.

• Must have high “sense of urgency” and “know how” to escalate to proper channels.

• Working knowledge of modern logistics, material flow and improvement strategies and the ability to integrate those into the operation.

• Experience or working knowledge of SAP, knowledge of TMS / WMS functionalities is expected.

Preferred Qualifications

• Any other professional certifications will be of added advantage.

• Proven self-starter, change agent and influencer.

• Ability to operate in an environment of significant change and ambiguity.

Apply today to be part of what’s next.

We make the tech that enables the chips in devices which improve lives around the world. We do this with an eye to the future, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible through cutting-edge innovation, and driving the next wave of technological breakthroughs that shape how we live, work, and connect.

To learn more about ASM, find us at asm.com and on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

ASM is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, nationality, social or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, gender, gender identify or expression, marital status, pregnancy, political affiliation, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Rwanda Data Audit Supervisor (Fixed-term)
jobs.description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

About the Role

Seeking a Rwanda Data Audit Supervisor to ensure data accuracy and integrity, support reporting, and provide trusted insights to drive informed organizational decisions.

Responsibilities

Data Verification & Quality Control

• Conduct field data audits, data reconciliation, and quality control checks across Phase 3 research activities to identify and resolve data errors promptly.

Excel & Technical Data Management

• Clean, manage, and structure field datasets using intermediate Excel functions and formulas to maintain data integrity.

Stakeholder Reporting & Documentation

• Document and present qualitative and quantitative field findings in English and Kinyarwanda to keep Trial Owners and Data Teams aligned on quality standards

Field Support & Quality Coaching

• Collaborate closely with field teams to provide hands-on coaching on QA standards and optimize survey execution.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

• Bachelor's Degree in Data Management, Statistics, Information Technology, Agriculture, or a related field.

• Proven experience in data verification, data quality management, field auditing, and error identification.

• Intermediate Microsoft Excel skills (pivot tables, data cleaning formulas, and basic calculations).

• Strong stakeholder coordination skills to liaise effectively between field teams, Trial Owners, and the Data Team.

• Demonstrated ability to document and report field observations accurately in both English and Kinyarwanda.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Muhanga, Rwanda

Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

Contract Duration

6 months Renewable

Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

Application Deadline

23 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

jobs.title: Senior Cryptocurrency Intelligence Scientist
jobs.description:
Do you want to be one of only a handful of people in the world able to programmatically detect and investigate complex on-chain criminal activity? Are you excited about deploying your data science skills at the cutting edge of cryptocurrency intelligence? Are you looking for a values-led company that trusts you to push the boundaries of what is possible in blockchain analytics?



The impact you'll have:
Join Elliptic's Intelligence team at the intersection of data science and blockchain analytics. As a Senior Cryptocurrency Intelligence Scientist at IC4 (Senior) level, you will become a go-to authority on on-chain attribution and threat characterisation, developing deep expertise in identifying patterns associated with specific entities, complex laundering techniques, and emerging criminal typologies. Your work will directly strengthen the intelligence dataset that underpins Elliptic's products, guiding our intelligence collection strategy and helping hundreds of financial institutions, exchanges, and government agencies understand and manage crypto-related financial crime risk. You will coach colleagues, collaborate across functions, and help deliver actionable intelligence to public-sector partners and the wider crypto industry.



What you will do:

 - Develop and own an expert understanding of identity and non-identity signals and data points necessary to characterise complex on-chain threats, going beyond wallet ownership to understand behavioural patterns, transactional rhythms, routing choices, bridge usage, and smart contract interaction patterns.

 - Lead end-to-end complex research and investigation efforts, from scoping and data collection through to written output, presenting findings rigorously and confidently to clients, partners, and internal stakeholders.

 - Evaluate Elliptic's attribution coverage across threat areas and lead projects that define and prioritise intelligence collection efforts, identifying where gaps are most material and driving durable remediation.

 - Develop processes and tooling that empower analysts and data scientists to actively contribute to the development of straightforward heuristics, including documentation standards, peer review processes, and monitoring for drift or degradation.

 - Maintain an opinionated, well-evidenced view of the future of cryptocurrency, the evolution of criminal typologies, and the emergence of new obfuscation techniques, and translate that into actionable intelligence priorities.

 - Summarise conclusions from your work into reports, briefings, and marketing content, calibrating depth and framing to the target audience.

 - Work closely with the Principal Cryptocurrency Intelligence Scientist and Professional Services team to deliver actionable intelligence to government partners and the broader crypto industry.

 - Build and invest in strong working relationships across Elliptic and develop good external relationships within the blockchain intelligence and financial crime research community.

 - Coach and mentor more junior colleagues, sharing technical and analytical expertise and contributing to a high standard of intelligence practice across the team.



What you will achieve in the first 6 months:

 - Establish deep familiarity with Elliptic's intelligence dataset and attribution methodology, and produce a documented assessment of the most material coverage gaps with a prioritised remediation roadmap.

 - Lead or contribute significantly to at least one end-to-end research or investigation project, delivering a defensible written output to an agreed standard and timeline.

 - Define and present a concrete proposal for improving how data scientists contribute to heuristic development, including documentation templates, review processes, and monitoring expectations.

 - Build strong working relationships with key stakeholders across Intelligence, Product, Engineering, and Professional Services, and identify at least one cross-functional opportunity to translate your intelligence work into product or client value.



You will be a great fit here if you

 - You are mission-driven and share our passion for securing the future of cryptocurrency.

 - You demonstrate a deep, active personal interest in the cryptocurrency space, staying current on developments across protocols, ecosystems, and criminal typologies.

 - You are enthusiastic about deploying your data science skills to explore new domains and solve problems that do not yet have established solutions.

 - You are familiar with OSINT techniques and understand the importance of operating safely, responsibly, and with rigorous attention to bias.

 - You are a collaborative team player who enjoys mentoring others and can work productively across functional areas including product, marketing, and customer success.

 - You take initiative and are comfortable operating with significant autonomy, owning your domain without waiting for direction.

Our ideal candidate has:

 - A strong understanding of data science fundamentals, with working knowledge of SQL and Python sufficient to conduct and automate analytical workflows independently.

 - Expert, demonstrable proficiency across a variety of blockchains, including layer 1 and layer 2 networks, with direct personal experience bridging cryptocurrency between chains and self-custodying cryptocurrency.

 - Competency as an intelligence professional: you understand the role of cognitive bias, can apply structured analytic techniques, and accurately communicate uncertainty in written and verbal outputs.

 - Excellent communication skills: you can distil complex technical matters clearly for audiences with a wide range of technical understanding, from engineers to executives.

 - Previous experience holding, or the ability to obtain, security clearance in the UK or US.

 - AI fluency is essential for this role. You must be able to demonstrate your ability to effectively apply AI tools and approaches to intelligence analysis workflows, including using AI to accelerate data processing, pattern identification, heuristic development support, and the drafting of written outputs.



Bonus points for:

 - Relevant postgraduate qualification in a technical or intelligence-adjacent discipline.

 - Experience working in a formal intelligence setting, including law enforcement, government, or academic research.

 - Commercial or research experience with cryptocurrencies, including complex transaction tracing, demixing, and cross-chain attribution.

 - Experience working for or with public-sector entities, including law enforcement or regulatory bodies.

 - Strong familiarity with key threat typologies, including thefts, scams, ransomware, nation-state activity, terrorism financing, and sanctions evasion.



Benefits:


> How we work:

 - Hybrid working: The option to work from almost anywhere for up to 90 days per year.

 - Remote Work Budget: $650 budget to set up your home office space.

> Learning & Development:

jobs.title: Head of People & Performance
jobs.description:
OUR MISSION:

At Sunrise Robotics, we are dedicated to augmenting humanity through intelligent robotics. Our mission is to elevate the world of manufacturing by introducing intelligent, flexible robots that enhance human capabilities and existing machinery, ushering in the next era of production at higher quality, with less waste, and lower cost.



OUR VISION:

We see a future where every element of manufacturing, from design to assembly, is optimised with intelligent automation. Our vision is to integrate flexible robotic solutions, based on generic hardware and advanced software/AI capabilities, into manufacturing, particularly in small and medium-sized enterprises, to make automation economically viable and accessible, for all sizes of manufacturers. We are not just building robots; we are creating the strategically crucial components for autonomous, intelligent agents of the future.

The role

We are hiring our first Head of People & Performance.

You report to the CEO and sit on the leadership team. You own how we hire, how we set the bar, how we review performance, pay and promote, and how we part ways. You also own the platform underneath: contracts, onboarding, HRIS and compliance across more than 10 European countries.

We have doubled the team in the last 9 months to 50 people today and expect to continue growing the team on a similar trajectory. The job is to build the people system that scales with that.

This is primarily a builder's role. Build lean - sharp systems, a small set of trusted partners, and automation for the transactional work. Grow the People team only when necessary.

We are outcome-driven, direct, high trust and high autonomy organization. There is very little hand-holding. We enjoy working with people that bring a healthy degree of intensity and drive.

 

What you will do

 - Own performance
   Design one performance cycle for the whole company and run the first one. Every leader should be able to tell you and the CEO who is above the bar, who is on it, and who is below, and act on it within days.

 - Own the employee experience
   Build what it is like to work at Sunrise from the first day to last.

 - Own compensation and levels 
   Build comp bands for today's roles, not a framework for roles we don't have yet. Hang them off a light leveling structure. Standardize pay awards and equity top-ups, so every hiring manager can make a defensible offer inside the system.

 - Own how we hire
   Manage our internal recruiting, embedded recruiting partners, and the hiring managers' process. Standardize scorecards and interview packs. A role does not open without one. You are not the recruiter, but you own the system the recruiters run in.

 - Own people operations end-to-end
   Contracts, onboarding, offboarding, HRIS, employer of record, policies, benefits by country, payroll inputs. Automate whatever can be automated. From signed offer to laptop on desk, no manual steps.

 - Coach
   Coach our leadership and team leads on people and performance: setting expectations, giving direct feedback, running hard conversations, acting early.

 - Codify our culture
   Talent and culture are upstream of everything else. The founders write it down. You turn it into how we hire, review and reward, and you act decisively when someone does not live it.

 - Keep us compliant across more than 10 countries
   Employment structure, ISO documentation. Own the framework that decides where and how we employ the best talent.

Who you are

 - You have built this before
   Somewhere, a fast-growing company runs on a people system you built. You may have been the first people hired at a Series A that grew past 100, the number two in a people function at a larger scale-up, or an operator who did it from a consulting, operations, or venture seat without the title. We care about the work, not the title.

 - You are a systems thinker
   You see how changing one thing here moves another thing there, and you design for it. You have built systems that survived scale while keeping the operation flexible.

 - You are not afraid of numbers
   Comp bands, equity, headcount plans. You are at home in a spreadsheet, and you never mistake the spreadsheet for the person.

 - You have operated across countries
   Employment complexity in more than 10 jurisdictions is a problem you know how to work with, not one you outsource entirely.

 - You are detail-oriented and write everything down
   You are bothered when small details don’t match. You are a great writer who values concise, legible, high-signal documents.

 - You hold confidences
   You will know things few others know. That access is a duty, not a way to be liked.

 - You push back on founders
   You get to the real intent behind a vague request and tell us when we are wrong.

 - You are curious about the work itself 
   You understand what a robotics engineer or a deploy engineer actually does day to day.

 - You set standards by doing 
   You are direct in 1:1s and you move fast. You are familiar with modern (AI) tools and best practices.

Bonus points

 - You know Deel, Shapes and Ashby, or their equivalents.

 - You have automated people-ops work with AI tools yourself, not bought a tool that promised to.

 - You have done this in a hardware or deep-tech company, where part of the team works next to the machines and part works in customer factories.

Why Sunrise?

 - Join an early stage team to work directly with the CEO, leadership, and founders in a high impact role.

 - We care about talent density, speed of execution, and long-term technology leverage.

 - Get things done and shape your own trajectory.

We believe the delivery service industry in its current state is massively under-serving merchants, and we are committed to creating a sustainable, reliable, and frictionless delivery experience for merchants and their customers.

Coco is a venture-backed, Series A stage startup that operates hundreds of sidewalk robots, delivering to thousands of customers every week across Los Angeles. The environment here is high-energy, collaborative, and exciting. Our HQ is located in Venice, CA.

About the Role

As a Software Engineer, you will be responsible for owning and driving products from design to development to testing to production. You will work closely with product managers to understand the needs of users (merchants, consumers, and internal stakeholders), propose technical solutions, structure and manage projects for junior engineers, and report on impact.

Note: This is an in-office role. Coco is an office-first, highly collaborative and cross-functional company. We are looking for someone who is excited about the energy, collaboration, and culture-building opportunities of an in-office work environment.

About the Team

As an engineer on the Delivery Platform team, you’ll build software products that power our delivery operations. This is a diverse team of engineers that owns every part of the stack. Our responsibilities include:

 - Consumer and Merchant Products: We build products to create a frictionless, efficient, and delightful end-to-end delivery experience for our users - merchants and their customers. We design each robot interaction - loading the robot, tracking the delivery, unlocking the robot, etc. around user pain points and moments of delight.

 - Order Ingestion: We build and manage the software partnerships that allow Coco to receive orders from all major ordering platforms including DoorDash, UberEats, and GrubHub and custom systems. Work on a variety of integrations and enjoy test orders from some of your favorite restaurants!

 - Delivery Management: We build backend services that make automated decisions based on user behaviors, supply/demand, government regulations, sidewalk conditions, and more.

 - Logistics: Delivery is an expensive problem. We partner with other Coco teams (e.g., Merchant Operations, Consumer Experience, Field Operations, TeleOperations, and Autonomy), acting as a thought partner to tackle some of Coco’s most pressing efficiency and profitability initiatives.

 - Internal Tools: Our software enables human operators to manage a fleet of delivery robots. We maintain a mobile native app for our Field Operations team and a web app for our remote Pilots to manage assigned deliveries.

 - Device Infrastructure: To operate as efficiently and reliably as possible, the above systems all need access to low latency, accurate robot telemetry. We architect and build backend services that communicate with devices and track information such as health, battery status and location.

Our Stack

Golang, Typescript, Postgres, RabbitMQ, Kafka, AWS, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Datadog

Basic Qualifications

 - BS in Computer Science or equivalent technical experience

 - 2+ years of professional software development experience

 - Experience designing and leading the implementation of new platform features and services, including their deployment in AWS

 - Experience supporting business-critical services in production (1+ yr)

 - Experience developing backend services in Go (preferred) or strong fluency in a comparable ecosystem like Python, Java, Rust, or C++, with a willingness to work primarily in Go

 - SQL database fundamentals (1+ yr)

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with at-least one message queue or pub/sub framework such as Kafka or RabbitMQ 

 - Experience with Kubernetes

 - Experience working in a startup environment

Coco is an Equal Opportunity Employer – Minority / Women / Disability / Veteran / Gender Identity / Sexual Orientation

jobs.description:
**This is a Full Time position at 40 hours per week for the Neurosurgery clinic located at Lake Forest Hospital. Schedule is Monday through Friday.**

The Medical Assistant reflects the mission, vision, and values of Northwestern Medicine, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Medical Assistant is a member of the health care team primarily responsible for providing support to physicians, nurses, and other licensed medical staff by facilitating efficient patient flow, assisting with various patient care activities, and performing related administrative functions. The Medical Assistant is responsible for ensuring efficient patient flow through the clinic; maintaining neat, clean and safe patient care areas; promoting patient satisfaction by interacting with patients in a professional, friendly manner; safeguarding patient confidentiality.

Responsibilities:

• Assures efficient patient flow through the site: Escorts patient to exam room, identifies patient with 2 identifiers and prepares patient for examination. Obtains accurate vital signs, per organization standards. Documents reason for visit and updates/confirms, allergies, smoking history and pharmacy information. Promptly informs the provider and registered nurse of any significant change in vital signs or acute symptoms. Anticipates/sets up equipment or supplies needed for visit. Cleans and prepares exam room for next patient. Responds to needs to expedite visits and maintain flow of patients and prioritize tasks accordingly.

Participates in environmental safety rounds. Maintains vaccine/medication inventory. Monitors and maintains equipment and instruments according to clinic guidelines. Assists in ordering supplies and correctly disposes of all expired items. Adheres to office opening and closing procedures.

Offers assistance to others. Attends and participates in staff meetings. Communicates appropriately and effectively with patients and patient care team (in the office and on the phone)

jobs.title: DRC Rotational Senior Associate / Manager (Fixed-term)
jobs.location: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo or Kimpese,  Democratic Republic of Congo
jobs.description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

It is estimated that 1.1 million hectares of forest land are being lost each year in the Democratic Republic of Congo. This pattern of deforestation, which has significant implications for the region, is primarily attributed to small-scale farming practices. One Acre Fund is working to address the root causes of deforestation, linked to poverty and low agricultural yields, by giving smallholder farmers the tools they need to shift their agricultural activities away from forest land and help them obtain bigger and healthier harvests. We train farmers in agroforestry, support the set-up and scale up of farmer-led entrepreneurial ventures, and operate along the seed value chain to ensure access to improved inputs for smallholder farmers.

About the Role

We are seeking dynamic and versatile professionals to drive high-impact cross-functional projects across internal systems, field operations, R&D (Innovations and MEL), donor/government relations, and people operations at One Acre Fund DRC. This opportunity is ideal for someone who excels at building solutions from the ground up and is eager to accelerate their growth across diverse workstreams. Fast-track into a permanent leadership role within 6–12 months. Based in Kinshasa or Kimpese with rural travel.

Responsibilities

Rotational Associates and Managers will be placed based on their strengths and alignment with these priority responsibilities.

Strategic Project Leadership & Cross-Functional Delivery

• Lead or support high-priority strategic initiatives assigned by senior leadership, coordinating across multiple teams and functions.

• Own project deliverables from scoping and planning through execution, monitoring progress, resolving bottlenecks, and adjusting course as needed.

• Provide short-term surge support to teams during capacity gaps, staff transitions, organisational pivots, or other priority periods.

• Build strong cross-functional relationships and contribute to organisational priorities with a high degree of initiative, accountability, and adaptability.

Research, Analysis & Strategic Insights

• Conduct rapid qualitative and quantitative research/analysis to inform programme strategy, operational improvements, and investment decisions.

• Assess new ventures and lead small program pilots

• Analyse programme, operational, and stakeholder data to identify trends, opportunities, risks, and actionable insights.

• Translate complex findings into clear recommendations, briefing notes, memos, presentations, and decision-support materials for senior leadership.

• Apply cost-benefit analysis, financial modelling, and budget/variance analysis to assess programme performance and support strategic decisions.

Operational Systems, Field Implementation & Innovation

• Identify operational inefficiencies and develop practical tools, workflows, and systems that improve collaboration, execution, and data use.

• Support field implementation through programme-area travel, data collection, program pilot execution, and operational research.

• Design, test, and document new interventions, systems, or processes, using field evidence and stakeholder feedback to recommend adaptation or scale-up.

• Onboard and coach field-facing teams on new tools, systems, and programmes while capturing lessons learned for institutional knowledge-sharing.

Partnerships, Business Development & Stakeholder Engagement

• Coordinate cross-functional inputs and contribute to high-quality proposals, concept notes, donor reports, and other external-facing materials.

• Liaise with DRC government counterparts and other strategic stakeholders on partnership priorities, ensuring effective internal coordination and follow-through.

• Facilitate workshops, learning sessions, and stakeholder meetings that strengthen collaboration, alignment, and shared ownership of priorities.

Rotational Development, Organisational Learning & Leadership

• Rotate across key departments during the first 6–12 months, contributing to functions such as supply chain, HR, finance, impact, and field operations.

• Develop a broad understanding of the DRC programme’s operating model, strategic priorities, and interdependencies across functions.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

• Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Finance, International Development, Agriculture, Social Sciences, Engineering, or another relevant field; a Master’s degree is an advantage.

• We welcome applicants from a wide range of fields, including consulting, development, humanitarian work, finance, HR, impact, sales, innovation, and science.

• 3 years' experience in project management, strategy, research, programme operations, consulting, business development, finance, or development-sector roles; greater experience and demonstrated independent leadership expected at Manager level.

• Understanding of programme implementation, operational challenges, and field realities in rural or low-resource contexts; agriculture or development-sector experience is an advantage.

• Proven critical thinking and problem-solving ability, with a track record of navigating complexity and driving clarity in ambiguous or fast-moving contexts.

• Strong analytical skills, either quantitative (e.g., financial modelling, performance analysis) or qualitative (e.g., research, synthesis, strategic insights).

• Innovative and resourceful mindset, with demonstrated ability to design or adapt solutions to operational or strategic challenges.

• Familiarity with the DRC operating environment, development landscape, or relevant regional context is an advantage but not required.

• Demonstrated ability to work across functions and locations, with willingness to travel regularly to programme areas and take on assignments based on organisational priorities.

• Professional fluency in English required; Basic French is an advantage; Lingala or other relevant local-language capability is an advantage.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Kinshasa or Kimpese, Democratic Republic of Congo.

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits.

Contract Duration

1 year, renewable with a high chance based on good performance.

Eligibility

This role is open to all applicants; however, candidates with citizenship or permanent residency in our Countries of Operations are strongly preferred.

Application Deadline

23 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis, which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.
