Innovate with purpose

At BILL, we believe in empowering the businesses that drive our economy. By replacing outdated financial processes with innovative tools, we help businesses—from startups to established brands—make smarter decisions and gain control of their operations. And we don’t stop there: we’re creating the future of financial automation so businesses can spend more time on what matters.

Working here means you become part of a vision-driven team that’s ready to tackle challenges and build cutting-edge solutions. We value purpose, drive, and curiosity—and we thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment. We're remote-first, with office spaces in San Jose, CA and Draper, UT — and opportunities to connect in person when it counts. BILLders collaborate to deliver real impact for businesses that need more time in their busy weeks.

BILL builds high performing teams and we seek to hire the best talent for every role. We're committed to building a workplace that fosters inclusion and diverse perspectives, valuing each person’s unique skills and experiences. We’d love to hear from you—you might be just what we’re looking for, whether in this role or another.

✨ Let’s give businesses more time for what matters.

Make your impact within a rapidly growing Fintech Company

Join BILL as a Staff Product Manager on our Payments and Financial Services team and own the product that determines how the company understands, reconciles, and acts on its financial data. BILL's FinSuite Platform team owns the core money-movement infrastructure that processes over $31.9B across 12 million payments per month, and Project TrueNorth is at the center of it: a unified financial ledger built to serve as the single source of truth for every dollar BILL moves across ACH, card, RTP, wallet, and international rails. The ingestion layer is live and in production. Now we need someone to build the other half of it.

In this role, you will own the Ledger Subscriber Ecosystem: the reports, dashboards, data products, portals, APIs, and workflows that turn the TrueNorth ledger from an internal system of record into the operating backbone for Treasury, Accounting, FP&A, Tax, Audit, Payment Ops, and every other finance function at BILL. This is not a consumer-facing role. Your customers are internal: the teams that run month-end close, produce regulatory reports, manage cash positioning, and prevent losses. You will define the 3-year subscriber platform strategy, drive workflow change across multiple senior finance stakeholder groups, ship iterative subscriber capabilities, and own outcome metrics that matter: reconciliation days reduced, manual recon hours eliminated, and the percentage of BILL's TPV operating on-ledger. Your work will directly shape BILL's audit posture, operational efficiency, and the speed at which finance teams can move.

Responsibilities:

• Define and own the 3-year vision, strategy, and roadmap for the Ledger Subscriber Ecosystem, translating Project TrueNorth priorities into a sequenced delivery plan across subscriber utilities, data products, reconciliation tools, and adoption milestones.

• Build and ship subscriber platform capabilities including L1/L2 reconciliation reports, exception and aging queues, cash positioning views, revenue and expense journal feeds into ERP and revenue systems, and ledger-backed data products for analytics and forecasting teams.

• Drive adoption of ledger-based workflows across Treasury, Accounting, and Payment Operations, replacing spreadsheets, manual reconciliations, and bespoke reporting with reliable, auditable platform tools.

• Act as the single-threaded owner for the subscriber ecosystem across Product, Engineering, Data Platform, Treasury, Accounting, FP&A, Tax, Audit, Legal, Payment Ops, Compliance, and CXO, running discovery with subscriber teams and converting findings into clear problem statements, specs, and PRDs.

• Represent subscriber needs in ledger architecture decisions, partnering with the Ledger Data Producer PM, engineers, and architects to ensure ledger schemas, events, and controls anticipate downstream use cases for reconciliation, reporting, compliance, and analytics.

• Set and own measurable outcome metrics for the subscriber ecosystem, including percentage of TPV and products operating on-ledger, reduction in reconciliation days, time to produce regulatory customer balance reports, and audit finding reduction.

• Communicate trade-offs, progress, and risks clearly to executives and senior stakeholders through written narratives, design reviews, and status updates, and mentor other PMs as a thought partner on ledger strategy and financial data.

We'd love to chat if you have:

• 8 or more years in Product Management, with at least 4 years in fintech, payments, financial systems, or enterprise SaaS focused on financial data, reconciliation, ledgering, or treasury.

• Direct experience building products for internal finance or operations users, specifically Treasury, Accounting, FP&A, or Payment Ops, where the deliverable was a workflow, data product, reporting surface, or API rather than a consumer-facing feature.

• Deep understanding of financial data flows and processes: ledgering and sub-ledgers, bank and GL reconciliation, month-end close, revenue recognition, or treasury and cash management.

• A track record of platform delivery where you owned the vision, wrote PRDs that engineering shipped from, drove end-to-end execution, and tracked outcomes with real metrics you set and baselined yourself.

• Proven ability to lead cross-functional programs that include Finance, Risk, Compliance, or Legal stakeholders, influencing senior leaders and driving workflow change without formal authority.

• Clear, structured written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex financial and technical topics in plain terms and write executive narratives that surface trade-offs and risks explicitly.

Desired Qualifications:

• Experience building on top of financial ledger systems, GL and sub-ledger platforms, or double-entry accounting infrastructure, including familiarity with vendors such as Fragment or Modern Treasury, or exposure to event-driven data architectures like Kafka or Flink in a financial systems context.

• Background in treasury, accounting, or FP&A, whether through a prior role or a close multi-year partnership, along with working familiarity with SOX controls, audit requirements, or regulatory reporting.

• Prior experience in B2B payments, BaaS, card platforms, or working capital products, particularly where processor settlement reports from Stripe, Chase, Adyen, or Marqeta were used for revenue recognition, cost of sales, or cash positioning.

Please note that this position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must have authorization to work in the United States without requiring visa sponsorship now or in the future.

jobs.title: Customer Service Operations Specialist
jobs.description:
THE PROBLEM



36 million businesses in America need insurance—it's not optional. 77% are underinsured. 40% have no coverage at all. The distribution system failed them: too slow, too opaque, too confusing.



Over 90% of commercial insurance is still human-led. We're building the inverse: 90%+ AI-led, pushing toward the higher 90s. Not by patching legacy workflows—by building AI that makes humans more effective, improves the customer experience, and eliminates friction at every step.



We're adding ~1,000 customers per month. We've grown 100x since last year. We're looking to do even more this year—and that's why we're hiring.



The accounts that need an expert instead of a script—those are yours.




THE THESIS



Commercial insurance gets complicated fast. A business opens a second location, wins a contract with insurance requirements it doesn't currently meet, adds a fleet, gets hit with a premium audit, grows out of the market it started in, or needs coverage that doesn't exist on a standard form. Those accounts don't need a queue. They need somebody with deep expertise and the latitude to act on it.



That's this team. You take the accounts that call for real judgment, you work them directly with the underwriters and wholesalers, and you stay on them until the customer has an answer. Then your expertise becomes the playbook the rest of the service organization runs on, which is how a small team serves a book growing this fast.



We're also building this tier now rather than handing you someone else's version of it. Harper's long-term plan puts service at the center of the company—expertise, retention and revenue all living in one organization—and the specialists we hire first will shape what that looks like.




THE ROLE



You own our most complex accounts and the hardest customer situations. Premium audits and inspection recommendations that carry real deadlines. Renewals worth remarketing to get a business better terms. E&S and surplus lines placements, with the filings and binding packets that come with them. Premium finance arrangements and the paperwork behind them. 



Coverage questions that need someone who can read a policy form and a contract and explain what's actually covered. And the accounts at risk of cancellation, where somebody's coverage is genuinely on the line and a customer needs a person who will solve it.



You own relationships too. Every underwriter and wholesaler we work with has a named owner on this team, and you'll be one of them. You're the person they pick up the phone for—and the person who can get a real answer for a customer because you've built that credibility over years.



You're the last stop inside service, which means nothing you pick up gets handed to somebody else to figure out. You have the latitude to make the call, and when something genuinely needs a founder's decision you bring it to them with your recommendation attached. Complex cases get answers in days here, not weeks.




WHAT YOU'LL DO



 - Own the complex accounts end to end — The situations that need experience rather than a script; you keep them until the customer has a real answer

 - Work the markets on your customers' behalf — Partner with underwriters and wholesalers to place hard risks, remarket renewals for better terms, and find a home for businesses standard markets won't write

 - Guide customers through audits and inspections — Premium audits, payroll and sales verification, inspection recommendations with deadlines; make sure the final number and the required changes are right and understood

 - Handle E&S and surplus lines work — Eligibility, filings, surplus lines tax, binding packets, and the documentation that has to be correct the first time

 - Make coverage match the business — Businesses change constantly: new locations, vehicles, payroll, equipment, and contracts with new requirements; keep coverage, class codes and records current as they grow

 - Save accounts worth saving — Work payment, financing and cancellation situations with the customer and the finance company so coverage stays in force

 - Be the name your carriers know — Own specific underwriter and wholesaler relationships and build the kind of credibility that gets customers a better outcome

 - Level up the team around you — Turn what you know into playbooks, train the service team, and grow the tier-two group into people who can handle more every month

 - Make the system smarter — Work in our service workbench daily and tell Product and Engineering what to automate, so your expertise scales past your own calendar




YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF...



 - You're the person colleagues bring the case nobody else can crack

 - You have real relationships with underwriters and wholesalers—and they take your call

 - You'd rather decide with the facts you have and document your reasoning than let an account sit for three weeks

 - You're tired of needing three approvals to do the obviously right thing

 - You can hold a case open for days without losing the thread, and keep twenty of them straight

 - You're curious about AI tools and want to tell engineers what to build, not wait for permission

 - You want to build this function, not inherit someone else's version of it

 - You know startup pace is a real adjustment from a traditional brokerage and you want it anyway




REQUIREMENTS



 - 5+ years in commercial lines underwriting, account executive, wholesale brokerage, or carrier-side roles

 - Active property & casualty license—we handle non-resident and reciprocal licensing across all 50 states

 - Existing carrier and wholesaler relationships you can put to work

 - A track record owning complex commercial cases end to end, not just triaging them

 - Comfort with technology; you'll work in our service workbench daily and be expected to tell us where it falls short

 - Based in New York City or San Francisco, or willing to relocate; this role is in-office




NICE TO HAVE



 - Surplus lines license

 - E&S experience: surplus lines tax, filings, binding packets, DocuSign workflows

 - Premium finance depth: PFAs, reconciliation, finance-company defaults and cancellation reversals

 - Workers' comp and class-code expertise, including NCCI audit disputes

 - Wholesaler, MGA or carrier underwriting-desk background

 - Experience at an insurtech or tech-forward brokerage




COMPENSATION



 - Salary: $110,000–$150,000 + performance bonuses + equity

 - Location: San Francisco, Atlanta, or New York City, in-office

 - Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8 AM – 8 PM ET. The hours are long. The learning curve is steep. The people who thrive here wouldn't have it any other way.

 - Start date: Immediate




BENEFITS



 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - Commuter benefits

 - Team meals and snacks




THE PROCESS



 1. People screen — Initial fit and alignment

 2. Founder screen — Insurance judgment, operating instinct, and culture fit

 3. Super day — Work through real cases with the team and see how you operate




TO APPLY



If you've spent years making the hard calls and watching them get second-guessed by people who couldn't make them, this is the seat where the decision is yours. Send your resume and tell us about the messiest commercial account you ever untangled—what was wrong, who you had to move, and how it ended.

jobs.title: Field Support Engineer
jobs.description:
OUR MISSION  


SPAN IS ENABLING ELECTRIFICATION FOR ALL ⚡

 


WE ARE A MISSION-DRIVEN COMPANY DESIGNING, BUILDING, AND DEPLOYING PRODUCTS THAT ELECTRIFY THE BUILT ENVIRONMENT, REDUCE CARBON EMISSIONS, AND SLOW THE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE.

 

 - Decarbonization is the process to reduce or remove greenhouse gas emissions, especially carbon dioxide, from entering our atmosphere.

 - Electrification is the process of replacing fossil fuel appliances that run on gas or oil with all-electric upgrades for a cleaner way to power our lives.
   
    


AT SPAN, WE BELIEVE IN:

 - Enabling homes and vehicles powered by clean energy

 - Making electrification upgrades possible

 - Building more resilient homes with reliable backup

 - Designing a flexible and distributed electrical grid





THE ROLE

Want to save the world from climate change? And to ride in with a superhero cape to solve tricky customer issues? If you love the adventure of working for a fast-paced startup and enjoy solving new challenges each day, look no further. SPAN is hiring a Service Engineer.

Sitting within SPAN’s Operations group and reporting to our Service Engineering Manager, you will join a team of fellow Service Engineers. The Service Engineering team has two charters. One is to be the Tier 3 escalation point for our Tier 1 and 2 customer support team for resolving technically complex product issues in the field. The second is to manage our field service dispatches by coordinating with installers and homeowners.

Your objective is to deliver excellent service to our technically-minded installers and our non-technical homeowner customers. You will need to be a strong partner to customer support and a bridge to various engineering teams all while driving technically challenging issues to resolution with a strong sense of urgency. A SPAN Service Engineer is patient, has a generalist’s mindset, and is an excellent technical problem solver.




RESPONSIBILITIES


TROUBLESHOOTING AND CUSTOMER SERVICE

 - Respond within the agreed upon timeframe (SLA) to issues escalated from Tier 1 and 2 and to responses from customers

 - Shepherd issues through to resolution with a sense of urgency, coordinating with all the necessary partners, including support, engineering, customers, and installers.

 - Collaborate with teammates on handling challenging troubleshooting issues

 - Participate in feedback loops (e.g. retrospectives) with Engineering and Customer Support

 - Use non GUI product access paths and tools (SSH, CLI) for higher level troubleshooting

 - Create and run basic scripts and light coding for queries into the product and various databases

 - Using a systems mindset, mine data and coalesce multiple site issues into one coherent problem statement

 - Build deep technical knowledge of our products and continuously deepen your own technical skills

 - Document and teach what you know to fellow Service Engineers

 - Embrace a continuous improvement mindset and suggest ways for the team to improve. This might mean suggesting new features for our internal troubleshooting tools, improvements to our core products, or changes to our SOPs

 - Contribute to the build out of out our library of troubleshooting documentation

 - Coordinate with your teammates to ensure we hit our coverage targets

 - Ensure clean handoffs between shifts through clear notes, and strict process adherence


ABOUT YOU


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 You…

 - Have 2+ years of experience as a service engineer, product support engineer, or similar role

 - Have experience working within a ticketing tool (e.g. Zendesk, JIRA, Salesforce, etc.)

 - Have experience troubleshooting networking issues and/or IoT devices

 - Have experience working in Linux systems

 - Have experience with SQL and command line interfaces

 - Are an excellent problem solver and possess a demonstrated ability to solve complex technical problems with a sense of urgency

 - Easily adapt your communication for different audiences (highly technical vs not technical)

 - Are deeply empathetic, enjoy speaking with customers, and bring a customer orientation to your work

 - Enjoy being a generalist and having your hands in a bit of everything

 - Bring an entrepreneurial spirit and a love of problem solving to every challenge you encounter

 - Are detail oriented, organized, and reliable. You do what you say you’re going to do and understand the importance of being the last point of escalation

 - Are a strong communicator, both written and verbally

 - Have a continuous improvement mindset

jobs.title: Customer Service Representative
jobs.description:
THE PROBLEM



36 million businesses in America need insurance—it's not optional. 77% are underinsured. 40% have no coverage at all. The distribution system failed them: too slow, too opaque, too confusing.



Over 90% of commercial insurance is still human-led. We're building the inverse: 90%+ AI-led, pushing toward the higher 90s. Not by patching legacy workflows—by building AI that makes humans more effective, improves the customer experience, and eliminates friction at every step.



We're adding ~1,000 customers per month. We've grown 100x since last year. We're looking to do even more this year—and that's why we're hiring.



Plenty of people can tell a customer what their policy says. You're licensed to change it.




THE THESIS



A business owner calls because they just won a job and the contract demands an additional insured endorsement by Friday. Or they bought a truck. Or they opened a second location. At most brokerages that starts a week of voicemail. Here it takes a licensed person who knows the product, can read the contract, and can make the change today.



That's the difference this role makes, and it's why this is the largest and most important group in our service organization. AI is taking the repetitive work off your plate—status lookups, standard certificates, document retrieval—so the licensed judgment is what's left. That's the part worth doing.



It's also the bench. Our specialists—the people who own carrier relationships and handle our most complex accounts—come from this team. We'll get you licensed in every state you need and back you to grow.




THE ROLE



You do the licensed service work: endorsements, certificates with real wording requirements, binding, coverage questions answered from the policy itself, cancellations and reinstatements, renewal preparation, audit intake, and billing corrections. When the front line can't resolve something without a license, it comes to you—and you finish it.



You work directly with carriers and wholesalers on routine service, and you'll learn their people and their portals quickly. You have genuine authority here: policy changes inside appetite, governed payment actions, reinstatement requests, and closing an issue once the work is actually done.



The pace is the real thing to know. Certificate wording and endorsements turn around inside a business day. A bind request goes out the day validation passes. A reinstatement request goes out the day the notice lands. When something needs coverage judgment or a different market, you pass it to a specialist with the history and evidence already assembled—a clean handoff, never a shrug.




WHAT YOU'LL DO



 - Keep policies current with the business — Endorsements for new vehicles, drivers, locations and equipment, plus limit changes inside appetite; a customer's coverage should never lag behind their growth

 - Get certificates exactly right — Additional insured, waiver of subrogation, primary and non-contributory, loss payee, notice of cancellation; read what the customer's contract actually requires and issue to match

 - Carry new business across the line — Validation, chasing subjectivities, bind requests, DocuSign and premium finance packets, policy delivery, and the binder-to-policy check that confirms it's real

 - Answer coverage questions from the policy — Open the form, read it, and explain in plain language what a business is and isn't covered for

 - Keep coverage in force — Cancellation notices, payment cures, reinstatement requests and autopay enrollment; a lapse is the worst thing that can happen to a customer

 - Prepare renewals properly — Exposure updates, loss runs, and flagging the accounts a specialist should remarket for better terms

 - Run audits and inspections at intake — Payroll and sales records, photographs, affidavits, scheduling and carrier-portal submission, so nothing stalls on a missing document

 - Fix billing — Refunds and corrections inside your authority, resolved rather than explained

 - Hand off complete, never half-done — When a case needs market or coverage judgment, the specialist gets the full timeline and evidence pack from you

 - Make the tooling better — You'll live in our service workbench; tell Product and Engineering what should be one click instead of twenty




YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF...



 - You're licensed in property & casualty, or you're ready to get licensed fast

 - You'd rather resolve the thing than route the thing

 - You can follow a playbook and speak up when the playbook is wrong

 - You're comfortable picking up the phone to an underwriter

 - You're accurate at speed—volume doesn't make you sloppy

 - You like knowing the product deeply, not just the process

 - You want to grow into a specialist who owns carrier relationships and the hardest accounts

 - You're curious about AI tools and want a say in what gets automated




REQUIREMENTS



 - 2+ years in commercial lines service, account management, or brokerage operations

 - Active property & casualty license, or the ability to obtain one quickly—we handle resident, non-resident and reciprocal licensing across all 50 states

 - Working knowledge of certificates, endorsements, and binding documentation

 - Ability to talk, type and navigate multiple systems at once without losing accuracy

 - Comfort with technology and genuine interest in working alongside AI tools

 - Based in New York City or San Francisco, or willing to relocate; this role is in-office




NICE TO HAVE



 - E&S and surplus lines exposure: filings, surplus lines tax, binding packets

 - Premium finance familiarity: PFAs, reconciliation, finance-company coordination

 - Workers' comp and class-code knowledge

 - Wholesaler, MGA, or high-volume commercial lines background

 - Bilingual (Spanish)

 - Experience at an insurtech or tech-forward brokerage




COMPENSATION



 - Pay: $75,000 - $95,000, depending on experience and licensing

 - Type: Full-time, exempt

 - Sign-on bonus: Available for strong candidates

 - Location: San Francisco, Atlanta, or New York City, in-office

 - Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8 AM – 8 PM ET. The hours are long. The learning curve is steep. The people who thrive here wouldn't have it any other way.

 - Start date: Immediate




BENEFITS



 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - Commuter benefits

 - Team meals and snacks




THE PROCESS



 1. Team lead screen — Skills and culture fit

 2. Manager screen — Alignment on pace and expectations

 3. On-site day — Meet the team, see the operation, work through real scenarios




TO APPLY



If you've spent a few years doing commercial lines service well and you're tired of a queue that never empties and a system that fights you, come do the same work with better tools and real authority. Send your resume and tell us about a customer you got covered when the deadline was tight.

jobs.title: Integrations Specialist
jobs.description:
Our Story

Campfire is a next-gen core accounting platform built for modern mid-market finance teams. We help them close fast and scale even faster. Our platform replaces outdated legacy ERPs and manual accounting processes with automation-driven solutions that simplify and accelerate finance workflows. In the past year alone, we have grown 10x, driven by strong customer demand and a product that delivers real results for accounting & finance teams. We are scaling quickly and building the future of finance by giving teams the clarity, control, and strategic visibility they need to lead with confidence.




ROLE SUMMARY

Campfire is hiring an Integrations Specialist to sit on the Implementation team and own the customer-facing side of integrations. Our customers typically migrate to Campfire from ERPs like NetSuite, QuickBooks, and Sage Intacct, then connect the systems they run every day - CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot, spend tools like Ramp and Float, billing platforms like Stripe, payroll providers like Rippling and Justworks, plus banks and data warehouses. You'll set up those connections, troubleshoot issues when they come up, and bring what you learn back to Product and Engineering. This role is for someone who understands how integrations work well enough to configure them, diagnose problems, and be a clear, credible bridge between customers, Implementation, and the engineers who build the underlying connectors.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Sit within the Implementation team and partner with Implementation Managers to set up integrations between Campfire and customer ERP/GL systems, banks, payroll providers, and data warehouses during onboarding

 - Configure and enable Campfire's existing integrations and data connections for customers — this role sets up and troubleshoots integrations rather than building new ones

 - Troubleshoot integration issues (sync failures, mapping errors, connectivity problems) and drive them to resolution, looping in Engineering when a fix needs new code

 - Serve as the point of contact and escalation resource for integration issues raised by Support, Customer Experience, or customers directly

 - Validate data accuracy after setup and during ongoing syncs

 - Document common integration issues, setup steps, and troubleshooting playbooks for internal and customer use

 - Gather and synthesize feedback on integration gaps and pain points, and take it to Product and Engineering to advocate for fixes and roadmap improvements

 - Represent the Implementation team's and customers' perspective in Product/Engineering discussions about integrations


REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years in an implementation, integrations support, or technical customer-facing role at a B2B SaaS or fintech company

 - Comfortable reading and reasoning about APIs, webhooks, and data mapping well enough to configure, troubleshoot, and clearly describe issues — not required to write integration code

 - Working knowledge of accounting/GL concepts (chart of accounts, journal entries, reconciliations, close processes), or the ability to learn them quickly

 - Familiarity with the ERPs customers migrate from (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage Intacct) and hands-on experience with the systems Campfire connects to - CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot), spend tools (Ramp, Float), billing platforms (Stripe), payroll providers (Rippling, Justworks), or bank feeds

 - Comfortable with SQL and structured data (CSV/JSON/XML) for diagnosing issues

 - Strong troubleshooting instincts — able to isolate whether an issue is data, configuration, or connectivity, and know when to loop in Engineering

 - Clear written and verbal communication; able to translate technical issues for both customers and internal Product/Engineering teams

 - Able to manage multiple concurrent integration setups in a fast-paced, high-growth environment


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with iPaaS/integration tooling (Workato, MuleSoft, Boomi, Zapier, or similar) as a user or configurer

 - Background in accounting, finance, or consulting (CPA or CPA-track a plus)

 - Experience with bank connectivity or treasury data feeds

 - Prior experience at a high-growth startup or an implementation-heavy SaaS company

 - Experience working cross-functionally with Product or Engineering teams to turn customer feedback into roadmap input

jobs.title: Manager, Customer Success
jobs.description:
A LITTLE ABOUT US

incident.io http://incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Netflix, Etsy, and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $96 million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.




THE ROLE IN ONE LINE

Lead and grow a high-performing, US-based CS team as we scale from $XXM to $XXXM, and beyond.




WHAT THAT LOOKS LIKE DAY TO DAY

You're our first manager of Customer Success in the US, and stepping into a unique scenario: you are not coming in to fix something — the team is already strong, and our retention metrics are the gold standard. Your job is to take what's working and make it repeatable — forecasting, renewals, customer health, the rhythms that hold up when the team is twice the size.

You'll lead CSMs across New York and San Francisco, spanning white glove, high and medium touch motions. You'll report into our CRO until we hire a global VP of Customer Success — a role we're actively working on — which means for now you've got a direct line to commercial leadership and unusual latitude to shape how the function runs. You'll have a counterpart running CS in EMEA, and the two of you will set the standard globally.

Expect to be a player-coach. You'll run forecast reviews and 1:1s, and you'll also be on customer calls — sometimes because an account needs you, often because you want to be close enough to the work to know whether the playbook you're writing actually holds. You'll partner tightly with Sales, Product, Marketing and RevOps, and you'll be one of the clearest voices of the customer inside the company, connecting what you're hearing in the field to where the product goes next.

We're AI-forward in two directions here. Our customers buy an AI incident response product, so fluency in what it does and where it's going is part of the job. And internally, we expect you and your team to be using AI in the actual workflow — account research, health signals, call prep, QBR prep — and to push that further rather than wait for someone to hand you a process.




SUPPORTING YOU

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

 - Market-leading private medical insurance. The proper kind, so you're never weighing up your health against a bill.

 - Competitive PTO. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

 - First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

 - Enhanced 401k. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

 - Meaningful equity. We're rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

 - Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We're all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

 - Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we're doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

 - Two budgets that have your back. $1000 to invest in your setup, $500 a year to invest in yourself.

jobs.title: [DH] Engineering Manager, AI Observability
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Team

As AI training and deployments scale, the volume of data we need to monitor and understand is exploding. Our team uses Claude itself to make sense of this data. We own an integrated set of tools enabling Anthropic to ask open-ended questions, surface unexpected patterns, and maintain meaningful human oversight over massive datasets.
Our tools are widely adopted internally — powering ongoing enforcement, threat intelligence investigations, model audits, and more — and we're looking for an experienced engineering manager to help us both scale up existing applications and go zero-to-one on new ones.

About the Role

As an Engineering Manager for the team, you'll lead research engineers who design and build systems that let AI analyze large, unstructured datasets — think tens or hundreds of thousands of conversations or documents — and produce structured, trustworthy insights. The team works across the full stack, from core analysis frameworks through user-facing apps and interfaces.

This is a high-leverage role. The tools you build will be used by dozens of researchers and investigators, and directly shape our ability to measure and mitigate both misuse and misalignment.

Responsibilities:

• Lead the design and implementation of AI-based monitoring systems for AI training and deployment

• Extend and improve core frameworks for processing large volumes of unstructured text

• Partner with researchers and safety teams across Anthropic to understand their analytical needs, and prioritize the team's work to build solutions

• Develop agentic integrations that allow AI systems to autonomously investigate and act on analytical findings

• Contribute to the strategic direction of the team, including decisions about what to build, what to partner on, and where to invest

• Coach and support your reports to understand and pursue their professional growth

• Run the team's recruiting efforts, ensuring we can grow as quickly as we need

• Design processes that help the team operate effectively

You May Be a Good Fit If You:

• Are an experienced manager (at least 2 years) and actively enjoy people management

• Have 5+ years of software engineering experience, with meaningful exposure to ML systems

• Are excited about the problem of scaling human oversight of AI systems

• Are familiar with LLM application development (context engineering, evaluation, orchestration)

• Enjoy building tools that other people use — you care about UX, reliability, and documentation

• Can context-switch between deep infrastructure work and user-facing product thinking

• Thrive in collaborative, cross-functional environments

Strong Candidates May Also Have:

• Research experience in AI safety, alignment, or responsible deployment

• Strong people management experience: coaching, performance evaluation, mentorship, career development

• Experience recruiting for your team: predicting staffing needs, designing interview loops, evaluating candidates, and closing them

• Practical experience with both data science and engineering, including developing and using large-scale data processing frameworks

• Experience with productionizing internal tools or building developer-facing platforms

• Background in building monitoring or observability systems

• Comfort with ambiguity — our team is small and growing, and you'll help define what we become

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$405,000—$850,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Partner Enablement Specialist
jobs.description:
Our Story

Campfire is a next-gen core accounting platform built for modern mid-market finance teams. We help them close fast and scale even faster. Our platform replaces outdated legacy ERPs and manual accounting processes with automation-driven solutions that simplify and accelerate finance workflows. In the past year alone, we have grown 10x, driven by strong customer demand and a product that delivers real results for accounting & finance teams. We are scaling quickly and building the future of finance by giving teams the clarity, control, and strategic visibility they need to lead with confidence.

Role Overview

As Partner Enablement Specialist, your mission is to make sure every external implementation partner can deliver the Campfire standard as reliably as our internal team does. You'll take the training curriculum and standards developed for internal onboarding and adapt them for an external audience — building the certification bootcamps, materials, and ongoing support that keep partners accurate, confident, and self-sufficient. This is a hands-on, execution-focused role: you're not designing the overall onboarding architecture, you're the person who makes sure partners actually learn it, pass it, and keep up with it as the product evolves.

Key Responsibilities

Partner Bootcamp Delivery

 - Run scheduled Partner Bootcamps, adapting the internal onboarding curriculum into partner-facing training sessions, workshops, and materials.

 - Own the partner certification process: administer assessments, track completion, and issue certifications against the rubrics defined by the Product Enablement Manager.

 - Maintain a partner-facing knowledge base (guides, FAQs, troubleshooting docs) that mirrors internal SOPs but is tailored for external use.

Partner Readiness & Support

 - Serve as the first point of contact for partner questions during and after certification.

 - Monitor partner-led implementations for early signs of drift from the Campfire standard, and flag recurring issues back to the Product Enablement Manager.

 - Collect partner feedback on training gaps, confusing configurations, or product friction, and route it upstream.

Content Maintenance

 - Keep partner training materials in sync as product changes roll out — update decks, scripts, and guides in real-time under the direction of the Product Enablement Manager.

 - Help build out video modules and self-serve certification paths as the partner program scales.

Cross-Functional Coordination

 - Partner with the Head of Solution Consulting Partnerships and the Accounting Partnerships Lead to coordinate bootcamp logistics — aligning on scheduling, partner cohorts, and readiness timelines for each partnership track.

 - Work with the Accounting Partnerships Lead to ensure bootcamp content reflects the specific configurations and workflows accounting partners need to certify on.

jobs.title: Workplace Change Manager
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

Crusoe is growing fast, and growth means change — expanding real estate, new workplace products, and new processes and ways of working across our global portfolio. We're looking for a Change Manager to deliver the people side of these transformations, ensuring that every employee, team, and leader is equipped, informed, and confident to embrace changes in the workplace. This role is critical to Crusoe's momentum: by minimizing resistance and driving adoption, you'll directly help our teams embrace change as a source of strength rather than disruption.



You'll partner closely with the workplace team and cross-functional partners to build readiness strategies, craft compelling communications, and coach employees through transitions — using proven frameworks like Prosci ADKAR to guide your approach. The ideal candidate is a strategic communicator and empathetic influencer who thrives in ambiguity, builds trust across all levels of an organization, and is energized by helping people navigate change successfully.



What You'll Be Working On:

 - Typical workplace change management projects include new office openings, office expansions, workplace tool launches, and workplace process changes. Beyond corporate offices, you'll also drive change management across Crusoe's manufacturing sites and data centers. For each project, you'll lead the following end-to-end change management activities:
   
   - Change Impact Assessment: Conduct comprehensive analyses that compare current state with future state to deeply understand how a given change will impact people, processes, and systems.
   
   - Change Strategy & Roadmapping: Develop change management plans and timelines to keep transformation initiatives on track and aligned with broader project milestones.
   
   - Readiness Assessments: Evaluate organizational readiness for upcoming changes and identify potential gaps before they become obstacles.
   
   - Leadership Alignment: Partner with senior leaders and front-line managers to activate them as visible, credible change sponsors who model the way forward.
   
   - Stakeholder Engagement: Partner with employees across all levels and teams to ensure relevant stakeholders are involved in the change journey.
   
   - Communication Design & Delivery: Create clear, compelling multi-channel communication campaigns that keep employees informed and engaged throughout each transition. Draft communication assets, lead the asset review cycle, and ensure timely delivery of messages.
   
   - Training Collaboration: Design and deliver targeted training programs that build employee capability and confidence.
   
   - Resistance Management: Anticipate friction points, proactively identify adoption risks, and coach people managers to help their teams move through change with resilience.
   
   - Cross-Functional Partnership: Serve as a trusted daily contact for teammates, project leads, and stakeholders across the business, ensuring alignment on change initiatives.
   
   - Metrics & Reporting: Track qualitative and quantitative adoption metrics to measure success and demonstrate the initiative's impact on business goals.
   
   - Travel: 10% domestic and international travel to our global offices.



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - 5+ years of relevant experience in change management, organizational development, human resources, or project management.

 - Proven stakeholder influence in driving alignment and action without relying on direct authority.

 - Exceptional active listening skills, with the ability to read a room, surface concerns, and respond with empathy and clarity.

 - Comfort with ambiguity, adapting your approach as initiatives evolve and priorities shift.

 - Demonstrated experience leading change management for workplace or real estate projects, such as office moves, space redesigns, or facilities transformations.

 - Experience working as part of a collaborative workplace team, contributing to shared goals alongside cross-functional partners.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex change initiatives into clear, accessible messaging.

 - Experience driving change management in fast-scaling or high-growth technology companies.

 - Background partnering with executive-level sponsors on enterprise-wide initiatives.



Bonus Points

 - A Bachelor's degree in Organizational Psychology, Business Administration, Communications, or a related field.

 - Familiarity with Prosci ADKAR or other structured change management methodologies.

 - Management consulting experience.



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $110,000 - $145,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.



Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Head of AI Deployment
jobs.description:
ABOUT GRYPS

Gryps is an AI operating system for the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. Institutional owners such as hospital systems, universities, and airport authorities run multi-billion-dollar capital programs on data scattered across emails, spreadsheets, network drives, and disconnected systems of record. Gryps connects that information and gives owner teams an AI operating system for their capital programs, so they can find answers, manage risk, automate their work and make decisions faster.

We are a product-focused organization that dreams big and achieves those dreams. Our customers are large players in the construction industry. This is an opportunity to be part of a nimble team where every individual is an expert in their area. We work fast, iterate quickly, and create a product that transforms how our customers work through AI.

This is the place for you if you’ve worked in a role at the intersection of AI, automation, data analytics, construction tech, construction management, and innovative technology—and you’re looking for the next leap in your career. You will have direct influence over the growth of Gryps within customer organizations, our product roadmap, and impact on the Gryps bottom line.

We’re a growing company backed by Primary Ventures, LDV Capital, Pear VC, and other top investors. You will work directly with the CEO and our customers—large organizations that own and operate hospitals, universities, and public infrastructure.




THE ROLE

We're hiring a Head of AI Deployment to lead a team of 4–6 in turning Gryps deployments into measurable value for our customers. You'll own the full post-sale relationship: understanding each customer's program, designing the data strategy behind their deployment, identifying the use cases that matter most, guiding the implementation team to fast, repeatable time to value, and measuring the success of the deployment.

This is a player-coach role. You'll work directly with owner executives and program leaders while developing early-career professionals into strong implementers and advisors. You'll also be accountable for renewals and expansion, because customers who get real value are the ones who grow with us.




WHAT YOU'LL DO


LEAD AND DEVELOP THE TEAM

 - Manage, coach, and grow a team of 4–6 customer success and implementation professionals, many early in their careers. Set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and build their construction domain knowledge and client-facing confidence.

 - Build the playbooks, standards, and rituals that make delivery consistent: onboarding frameworks, implementation checklists, account reviews, and health scoring.


DEFINE VALUE AND DATA STRATEGY

 - Work with customers to find the highest-value use cases across their capital programs, such as cost and change tracking, schedule risk, document and contract intelligence, closeout, and portfolio reporting. Prioritize them by business impact and feasibility.

 - Design the data strategy for each use case: which sources to connect, how unstructured and structured data is organized and validated, and how outputs tie back to the customer's systems of record and decisions.

 - Turn customer outcomes into clear, quantified value stories that executives and champions can carry into their own organizations.


OWN CUSTOMER RELATIONSHIPS

 - Serve as trusted advisor and executive sponsor for your accounts, from project and program managers up to VPs of Facilities, Capital Planning, and Real Estate.

 - Lead executive business reviews that connect product usage to program outcomes and set the agenda for what comes next.

 - Represent the customer's voice internally, partnering with Product and Engineering on requirements, feedback, and roadmap priorities.


DRIVE PRODUCT ENGAGEMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION EFFICIENCY

 - Own adoption and engagement metrics across your book of business. Spot drifting accounts early and step in before they become risks.

 - Run implementation for speed and repeatability. Remove bottlenecks, standardize what can be standardized, and keep shortening time to first value and time to full deployment.


OWN RENEWALS AND EXPANSION

 - Own gross and net revenue retention for your accounts, including renewal forecasting, negotiation, and execution.

 - Find and close expansion opportunities such as new use cases, departments, programs, or campuses, working with Sales on commercial strategy and contracting.
   
   


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 8+ years of construction domain experience, with a deep understanding of how capital projects are planned, delivered, and closed out, and the data that flows through each phase.

 - An engineering or quantitative background, such as a degree in civil, mechanical, or construction engineering, construction management, or another analytical field, plus comfort reasoning about data structures, metrics, and systems.

 - Executive presence. You're credible with senior owner leadership, can run a boardroom conversation, and can hold a point of view under pressure.

 - A track record of coaching early-career professionals and building teams that measurably improve under your leadership.

 - Clear, structured communication, written and verbal. You explain complex technical and data concepts simply to field teams and executives alike.

 - Experience designing data strategies, or a proven ability to connect business problems to data sources, workflows, and outcomes.

 - Commercial ownership. You're comfortable being accountable for renewal and expansion revenue.
   
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience at an owner organization, such as a health system, university, airport, public agency, or large real estate owner, managing capital programs from the owner's side.

 - Experience implementing or managing construction technology platforms such as Procore, e-Builder, Unifier, Kahua, or enterprise data and AI tools.

 - Familiarity with BIM, digital twins, GIS or facilities and asset management data.

 - Experience at an early-stage or high-growth software company.
   
   


HOW SUCCESS LOOKS IN YOUR FIRST YEAR

 - Customers reach first measurable value on a predictable, shortened timeline.

 - Every account has a documented use-case roadmap and data strategy tied to executive-level outcomes.

 - Your team runs on shared playbooks, and each team member has grown noticeably in skill and independence.

 - Strong gross retention and meaningful net expansion across your book of business.

jobs.title: VP of Finance
jobs.description:
ABOUT LEAP

Leap is one of the fastest-growing benefits solutions and a category-defining pioneer in employer specialty pharmacy. We are reshaping how life-changing therapies are delivered and financed, ensuring patients get the treatment they need while employers finally get a fair deal.

Specialty drugs and infusions represent nearly 10% of all healthcare spend and are the fastest-growing cost category for employers. Leap tackles this challenge with a novel approach: eliminating hidden markups, expanding access to high-quality infusion providers, and bringing clarity and fairness to how therapies are priced and paid for.

We’re proud to partner with numerous Fortune 500 companies and leading TPAs. Each patient we serve creates immediate ROI: lower costs, improved access, and better care. Join us as we redefine what’s possible in specialty care.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Leap is growing quickly, and many of our most important decisions — where to invest, what to prioritize, how aggressively to spend, and how to allocate capital — depend on finance.



As VP of Finance, you will be the senior finance leader responsible for turning that ambiguity into clear decisions. You will own the operating model the company plans against, build the capital allocation framework that determines what we fund and in what order, and forecast the business when the answer is not obvious.



This is a leadership role with real influence over company strategy. You will lead core FP&A and revenue cycle finance from day one, recruit and build the finance organization as Leap scales, and partner closely with Growth Ops & Strategy, Client Ops & Success, and Member Growth. You will report directly to the President and help shape not only the analysis behind major decisions, but the decisions themselves.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Capital Allocation & Strategic Decisions

 - Build the framework Leap uses to decide where to invest, what to fund, and what to defer

 - Turn ambiguous, high-stakes questions into clear, defensible trade-offs for leadership

 - Own board materials and partner on fundraising, including the model, narrative, and diligence process

 - Help leadership evaluate major investments, hiring plans, client opportunities, and growth bets

Forecasting & Operating Model

 - Own the company operating model and ensure it becomes the source of truth for planning

 - Build client-level forecasts with clear assumptions, ranges of outcomes, and performance goals

 - Set ambitious but credible budgets and manage burn against plan

 - Create the financial visibility leadership needs to make faster, better decisions

Leadership & Team

 - Lead core FP&A and revenue cycle finance through your team

 - Recruit, manage, and develop the finance organization as Leap scales

 - Partner across Growth Ops & Strategy, Client Ops & Success, and Member Growth to pressure-test major bets

 - Build finance into a function the rest of the company relies on for fast, reliable answers




QUALIFICATIONS

Required

 - You are a strategic finance leader, not just an FP&A operator. You are strongest on the hard prioritization calls: where to invest, what to cut, and what to fund next.

 - You are comfortable with ambiguity. You can forecast a business when the answer is not clean, state your assumptions, and explain where the model may break.

 - You know how to build decision frameworks that leadership actually uses.

 - You think like an underwriter. You can size an opportunity, build the case, and stand behind the number.

 - You have led and built teams. You can recruit, manage, and grow a finance organization, not just do the work yourself.

 - You have 7–10+ years of experience in strategic finance, with a foundation in investment banking, investing, or an equivalently rigorous analytical environment.

Preferred

 - Investing experience in private equity, growth equity, or late-stage venture, especially where you underwrote deals and lived with the outcomes

 - Early-stage or high-growth startup experience

 - Healthcare, healthcare services, benefits, pharmacy, or revenue cycle exposure




COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary

 - Eligibility for equity

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

 - Access to 401(k) retirement plan

 - Flexible remote work



At Leap, we’re building an outlier company with real impact — and that takes focus, energy, and commitment. If that excites you, we’d love to hear from you.

Leap is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds. We’re committed to building a team that reflects a diversity of perspectives, experiences, and identities.

jobs.title: BDR Manager
jobs.description:
A LITTLE ABOUT US

incident.io http://incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Netflix, Etsy, and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $96 million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.




THE ROLE IN ONE LINE

Hire, train, and develop the future all-star sellers of incident.io http://incident.io.




WHAT THAT LOOKS LIKE DAY TO DAY

Starting in January, we're scaling the BDR team significantly. We'll hire in cohorts, target high potential, and invest heavily in the people who show it.

We're designing a comprehensive in-house training program for these future hires, but the program won't work without a proven people manager to lead it.

Our BDRs historically go on to become our commercial and enterprise reps, but we also see an opportunity to build pathways into other GTM functions, including: rev ops, solutions engineering, expansion account management, and CS.

We view the BDR org as the backbone of our hiring system. The quality of who you bring in and how fast you develop them is the number one priority of this role.

You'll also be our ears and voice at the top of the funnel. The trends your reps hear, the objections, the pushback, all of it needs to get to sales, marketing and product. You'll hold your team to account on follow-up and be marketing's point of contact for campaigns and events.

Of course you'll also own the pipeline number for your team. We care whether you're reaching potential champions inside our ICP whose pain we can actually fix, not whether the meetings-held count looked healthy on Friday.

Last but not least, we're also rethinking what a BDR is now that AI has removed most of the constraints the role used to carry. We think the modern BDR function is made up of highly agentic, first-principles thinkers limited mainly by their own curiosity. Part of your job is finding the plays that outperform, whether they're AI-driven or just creative, and turning them into how everyone works.




WHO YOU ARE

 - You've led a BDR or SDR team and it worked. Your team hit their numbers, the pipeline closed, and your reps got promoted.

 - You're strong at performance management. You hold a high bar, you're clear with people about where they stand, and you build development plans that get someone who's trailing back up to speed.

 - Developing people is the part of the job you'd do anyway. You want to build the bench as much as the board.

 - You've built something with AI that people actually use. You understand what today's tools do well and where they fall over, well enough to say how you'd attack a real problem with them even if someone else writes the code.

 - You have a fingertip feel for your own business and you're nosy about why things work.

 - You were a top-performing rep before you were a manager.

 - Ideally you've done this at a company selling technical products to engineering teams, in infrastructure, dev tools, observability or data platforms.

 - You're up for building something rather than inheriting it, from our San Francisco office.




SUPPORTING YOU

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

 - Market-leading private medical insurance. The proper kind, so you're never weighing up your health against a bill.

 - Competitive PTO. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

 - First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

 - Enhanced 401k. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

 - Meaningful equity. We're rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

 - Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We're all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

 - Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we're doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

 - Two budgets that have your back. $1000 to invest in your setup, $500 a year to invest in yourself.

Below are multiple positions across various disciplines that may be available, offering the chance to work on innovative projects for Summer 2027. Requirements

• Be currently enrolled or recently (2027) graduated with a Bachelor's or Master's Degree from an accredited university

Intern Position Descriptions

Core Thermal Hydraulics Intern

The CTH Intern will develop intermediate fidelity (IF) subchannel and high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models for applications in sodium fast reactors (SFRs). The project will involve comparisons between simulation results and experimental data. The exact topic will depend on interest and company needs but could cover fluid-structure interaction, turbulence model development, uncertainty quantification, or surrogate modeling.

• Required Qualifications Coursework in fluid mechanics and heat transfer Experience with 3-D CFD and meshing workflows Proficiency in Python Clear technical communication and documentation skills

• Bonus Qualifications Experience with advanced 3-D CFD concepts (large eddy simulation, fluid-structure interaction) Familiarity with high-performance computing workflows and tools Experience with MOOSE Familiarity with statistics and reduced order modeling

Fuel Performance Intern

Working with members of Oklo’s Materials and Fuel Performance Team, this intern will explore the potential of lower-order fuel performance models to help accelerate our core-design iteration.

• Key Responsibilities Assess the trade-off between computational cost and accuracy of lower-order fuel performance models Distill key phenomena for a variety of safety and design applications in order to calibrate simplified models against validation cases Benchmark new fuel performance tools Integrate original analysis and data processing into our production stack

• Required Qualifications Fluency in Python (or another object-oriented programming language) Prior experience with finite element analysis (FEA) Background in nuclear engineering and familiarity with reactor physics Motivated learner who is adept at efficiently summarizing literature

• Bonus Qualifications Exposure to the MOOSE modeling suite Strong understanding of statistics and/or uncertainty quantification Coursework or research related to materials science

Mechanical Analyst Intern

This intern will contribute to the evaluation and optimization of mechanical components that are critical to Oklo’s advanced power plant designs. This position offers hands-on experience in applying engineering fundamentals, performing structural analysis, and integrating results into design iterations.

• Key Responsibilities Apply first-principles mechanics and strength of materials to support analysis of structural components Assist in summarizing mechanical analysis results for design teams, highlighting key findings such as peak stresses, margins of safety, and potential design revisions Support the development of technical documentation, ensuring clear and concise communication of assumptions, methods, and results Collaborate with design, manufacturing, and testing teams to help inform design improvements

Instrumentation and Controls Intern

This intern will contribute to the development, integration, and testing of measurement and control systems that support advanced reactor operation and power generation. This position provides hands-on exposure to sensors, automation, and control strategies, while giving interns the opportunity to apply classroom knowledge to real-world engineering challenges.

• Key Responsibilities Assist in developing and testing sensors, instrumentation, and actuators under real design constraints Help design and implement control algorithms for equipment and processes Support the integration of I&C components into reactor systems and analysis workflows Contribute to documenting methods, results, and system designs in a clear and professional manner Collaborate with design and analysis teams to provide feedback that supports rapid iteration and improvement

• Required Qualifications Working toward a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field Familiarity with measurement techniques, data acquisition, and signal processing Exposure to control theory and feedback systems through coursework or projects Basic programming skills in Python (or similar) for data analysis and automation Strong communication skills and an eagerness to learn in a collaborative environment

• Bonus Qualifications Experience with circuit design (analog or digital) from labs, research, or projects Exposure to communication protocols and digital networks Familiarity with Git version control

Neutronics Methodologies Intern

• Required Qualifications Proficient in Python for scripting and automation. Familiar with AsciiDoc for documentation and formatting. Strong background in nuclear engineering and neutronics. Attention to detail with an ability to identify gaps in methodologies and processes.

Process Intern

• Required Qualifications Working toward a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a related discipline Background in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer through coursework or projects Familiarity with process or system modeling tools (e.g., MATLAB, Python, Aspen, or similar) Strong problem-solving skills with attention to detail Ability to clearly communicate technical findings through reports or presentations

• Bonus Qualifications Experience with lab work, prototyping, or experimental systems Exposure to piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs) or process design coursework Familiarity with pumps, heat exchangers, or thermal-fluid systems from research or internships

Prototyping/Manufacturing Intern

Business Operations Intern

This role is ideal for someone looking to grow their operational skill set in core business operational functions and is passionate about contributing to initiatives that drive efficiency while supporting key compliance functions across the organization.

• Key Responsibilities Assist with day-to-day business operations, including process documentation, workflow optimization, and project coordination. Collect, organize, and analyze operational and financial data to generate insights and support decision-making. Prepare reports, presentations, and dashboards for internal stakeholders. Collaborate with cross-functional teams (finance, HR, marketing, product, etc.) to support operational initiatives. Conduct research on industry trends, competitors, and best practices to support strategic planning. Identify and recommend opportunities for process improvements and increased efficiency. Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) or Google Workspace. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. Attention to detail and eagerness to learn.

Competencies

• Willing and able to learn quickly

• Eager to work on a dynamic team, receive constructive feedback, and grow with us

• Willing to think differently and do things in new ways

• Able to communicate technical content and results verbally

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

About Oklo's Intern compensation:

Oklo offers housing assistance, $35 - $44 per hour (compensation is determined based on education, skills, and experience), 1-on-1 mentorship, hands-on training, and the opportunity to engage in fun team-building activities as well as interactive workshops, enhancing both professional and personal growth.

Due to the nature of Oklo's work, only U.S. citizens can be considered for these positions.

About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

#CHOP: Oklo’s Values
Collaboration: We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
Humility: We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
Ownership: We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through  to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
Pathfinding: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.

Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer

Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address.

All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process.

If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

Sets the growth roadmap across digital and offline channels, leads the growth marketing team, and partners with the SVP of Marketing & Internal Communications, Product team, and IT to build funnels, launch products, and grow membership and share of wallet.
